The Place of Shining Rock.name: The Place of Shining Rock
The Place of Shining Rock.text:
On the road to Middenheim, about 50 miles from the city, there is a remote shrine known as the Place of Shining Rock. Unusually, it is sacred to both Ulric and Sigmar, and the two cults coexist here peacefully, as they have done for thousands of years.

The Place of Shining Rock features in Empire in Ruins (@UUID[JournalEntry.7w2yyQTWCPXye9DS]{chapter 3}), as the Characters attend a meeting between delegations from Altdorf and Middenheim. This chapter presents more detailed information on the shrine, along with some ideas that can be used to add complication to the events, or give Characters reason to return to the shrine at a later time.

These events serve to underscore the differences of opinion between the most stringent and outspoken Sigmarites and Ulricans, and can serve to underline this conflict. Conversely, the shrine is also a place of union between the two Gods. Spending time here may help to remind Characters who are strongly partisan towards one god or the other that compromise between the two faiths is an ideal worth striving towards.

Reaching the Shrine.name: Reaching the Shrine
Reaching the Shrine.text:
The Characters will visit the shrine during the events of Empire in Ruins, as delegations from Altdorf and Middenheim meet in an attempt to calm rising tensions between Ulrican and Sigmarite factions. However, during Power Behind the Throne they will also pass the site on their way to Middenheim, and it may help to add to the sense of gravitas the site enjoys if the Characters are already familiar with it before Empire in Ruins.

Any time that the Characters are travelling between Middenheim and Altdorf, they will pass by the road that leads to the Place of Shining Rock. Unless they have a reason to go there, though, they will probably overlook the place — they do have an Empire to save, after all. Here are a few possible ways to weave a visit to the shrine into the plot of the adventure, especially if you would like the Characters to visit it before Empire in Ruins.

Just Passing By

The Characters will have to travel between Altdorf and Middenheim at least once in the course of the campaign, which will take them past the side-road that leads to the shrine. If the party includes devout followers of Sigmar and/or Ulric, they may decide to visit, pay their respects, and pray — especially if one or more Characters has received Sin Points from either deity.

A Research Mission

By now, the Characters will no doubt be aware of the broad outlines of the doctrinal differences that have led to the growing conflict between the cults of Sigmar and Ulric. They may have learned part of the story from the scholar-monk @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus} in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.fzxPnClojPBcpfmA]{‘Vengeance of the Gravelord,’} or they may have picked up bits and pieces along the way.

They will probably have heard, as well, that Sigmarite and Ulrican scholars are combing through ancient records and later works of theology in the hope of finding an underlying truth upon which both sides can agree, and which can provide a basis for peace. As a shrine sacred to both gods, the Place of Shining Rock will be of great interest to these theologians.

In the course of their adventures, the Characters have become acquainted with one or more distinguished theologians. Sigmarites might be monks from @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus’s} monastery near Dunkelberg, or from the other renowned monastery at Priestlichheim, or scholars from the Department of Theology at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.EmhvOkkzAir6pzCB.JournalEntryPage.OiAVm63T9JEFsVfR]{University of Altdorf}. Their Ulrican counterparts will almost certainly be from Middenheim’s @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.PJSTe8IXwh6oy78t]{Collegium Theologica}.

Whatever their faith and wherever they come from, these scholars will need an escort on the dangerous highway through the Drak Wald, and although they expect that their research in the shrine’s archives will go smoothly and quickly, who is to say what they will find once they get there?

The Relic

The Characters are approached by priests of both religions, and asked to bring one chest of Ulrican relics and one chest of Sigmarite relics to the Place of Shining Rock, along with a sufficient cash donation to permit the expansion of the existing buildings and the construction of a new reliquary chapel. The priests’ aim is to promote peace between the two faiths by raising the profile of their shared holy place, highlighting its spiritual importance, and turning this sacred site into a popular destination for pilgrims.

Relics and Miracle

When using holy relics in a game, as the GM, you should take some time to design them. Every relic needs a form, a backstory, and specific effects, while the most powerful can require almost as much detail as an NPC, reflecting the aspects of their deity’s personality and interests that are channelled through them into the world. Like enchanted items and other supernatural objects, powerful relics are extremely rare in the Old World — but of course, there is no shortage of charlatans and other enterprising types who will be only too happy to sell a lock of Sigmar’s hair, a vial of Shallya’s tears, or a tooth lost by Ulric while fighting Daemons in the form of a wolf.

When a relic is genuine, it should have some supernatural effects that are in keeping with its patron’s personality and with a level of power appropriate for its size, form, and degree of sanctity. As GM, you have complete freedom to design relics according to the needs of your campaign, but here are a few ideas to help get you started.

For Grognards: A Stolen Shard

In @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.fzxPnClojPBcpfmA]{‘Vengeance of the Gravelord’} in the Death on the Reik Companion, the Characters encountered @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus}, a scholar-monk whom @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Harald Gräber}, the necromancer, tried to assassinate. In the original ‘Carrion Up the Reik’, Father Marcus revealed to the Characters that he had spent some of his time as a novice serving at the shrine, and when he left he took a tiny shard of the stone with him . As time went on he felt more and more guilty about it, and resolved to make a pilgrimage to return the shard to its rightful place. However, he was prevented from doing so by pressing concerns elsewhere, and asked the Characters to return the shard for him.

If you are reading this before you have run Power Behind the Throne, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus} could give the Characters this little quest while they are travelling together on the river. The Characters might stop off on their way to Middenheim during Power Behind the Throne, although they will probably not want to delay their journey. They might tell themselves that they will keep their promise to the kindly old monk on their way back to Altdorf — which, of course, would be in Empire in Ruins.

Of course, there is always the chance that @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus} survived the Gravelord’s attack on the Characters’ boat, and their paths crossed at some other point in the campaign. So long as the Characters’ immediate travel plans will take them along the Altdorf to Middenheim road, he can still ask them for the same favour. Even if Father Marcus is dead, the Characters might run into his two subordinates, @UUID[Actor.tCDLCDRYyPyNkFzB]{Brother Martin} or @UUID[Actor.8xYAPlRLgbNOq519]{Brother Rolf}, who tell them of the good Father’s dying wish that the shard be returned to its rightful place.

Of course, there are those who want to prevent this from happening. Some fanatics, when they hear of the plan, will stop at nothing to seize the relics, intending to take those of their own god to a suitable, unshared temple. The relics of the rival deity are regarded as heretical and must be destroyed. Bandits will be happy to relieve the Characters of the cash donation, and will probably find some sale value in the relics as well. They may pretend to be followers of one deity or the other in order to disarm the Characters’ suspicions and get close enough to attack.

The relics themselves are secured in stout chests and protected by multiple locks. They may be genuine, and may even have some religious power (see Relics of Note). More likely, they will be fakes: harmless bones and other objects that have become associated with a particular legend from the lore of one of the gods, but which are, in fact, completely mundane and unrelated.

Some relics are deliberate fakes, while others may have been given to a temple in the honest belief that they are genuine. Worst of all, the relics may actually be artefacts of Chaos, and the priests who approached the Characters may be cultists in disguise. Upon reaching the shrine and opening the chests, the Characters may find themselves faced with Warpstone that bathes them all in deadly radiation, or Daemons cast into the forms of ancient objects — a form that will be dispelled by the holy ground of the shrine.

The Aura of Sanctity

Some relics give off an aura that can be felt by those with Second Sight. It confers one or more Talents on any Character holding it, provided they are followers of the same deity. Suitable Talents include @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.QyjWtSdnVMT04l5Y]{Bless}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.x8g3U68oi8XzWiYr]{Commanding Presence} (vs followers of the same deity), @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.8pVzgPkgWpTJvfhG]{Fearless} (vs followers of Chaos or a rival deity), @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.mqo51ORnxijcqNNu]{Frightening} (vs followers of Chaos or a rival deity), @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.RyxOZqcBNZ7Zw721]{Holy Hatred}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Nj3tC8A5fZ3zEdMR]{Holy Visions}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.oGbDwnLOn3isPJpO]{Impassioned Zeal}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.WCXnFSV4WOSmzzc4]{Inspiring}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.voV0C2ar1bKpcpnH]{Invoke}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.wNvPXAhlKABl6hpk]{Pure Soul}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.IogM5gnsoOX63w7j]{Stout-hearted}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.Ywo6fZNPC4zbHHSQ]{Strong-minded}, or any other Talent that seems appropriate to the relic’s form and the deity’s interests.

The Power of Prayer

A relic can empower its wielder’s prayers, adding 1–3 SLs to the result of any Pray Test to the deity in question. Rolls on the @Table[wrath]{Wrath of the Gods Table} have a modifier between –10 and –30: a result of zero or less means that the Wrath of the Gods has been avoided.

Signs of Favour

When a Pray Test for a Miracle is successful, the Character gains a Blessing of the patron deity (GM’s choice) in addition to the Miracle they sought. If the Test is a Critical success, two Blessings are gained.

Relics of Note

The Skull of Englebrecht the Wise

Englebrecht the Wise was a scholar of Sigmar who died in 1450 IC. A devout worshipper and acomplished scholar, Englebrecht spend much of his life in a small monastry near Desidorf, compiling notes on the various histories of Sigmar, writing theological missives, and caring for a small collection of chickens. Englebrecht eventually died when a candle he was writing by tipped over, burning down much of the monastry. The only surviving artefacts from Englebrechts room were his skull, miraculously unmarred by the flames, and his final writings. Though a minor figure in the church, Englebrecht's skull is nevertheless a holy object. Anyone possessing the skull is immune to the @Condition[Ablaze] condition.

The Axehead of Margritte

A warrior priest of Ulric, Margritte died in Brettonia during one of the many campaigns the Empire has fought there. The axehead is all that remains of her weapon, shattered upon the enchanted armour of a grail knight. Though now ruined, the fragmets of the axehead carry a potent mote of Margritte's unwavering faith in Ulric. Anyone bearing even a piece of Margritte's axe adds +1 to the damage of any axe they weild.

Shard of the Shining Rock

A tiny fragment blasphemously removed from the relic of Shining Rock, this piece of black obsidian has now power of its own. However, should it be returned to the shrine by a devotee of either Sigmar or Ulric, that person may remove any Sin Points they have currently accumulated. If they have no Sin Points, they may instead add the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.QyjWtSdnVMT04l5Y]{Blessed} Talent to their current career.

The Priests' Quarters

This low, plain building accommodates the shrine’s complement of a dozen priests: six from each faith. Unusually, the Place of Shining Rock does not have any guest accommodation. Visitors are encouraged to pray in the shrine, leave a donation, and continue their journey. The priests have no objection to visitors pitching tents in the clearing for a night or two, but anyone planning on staying longer will arouse their suspicions. The shrine is a simple one, and there is nothing much to do here once one has prayed and donated.

The Hall

Double doors open onto a common hall and refectory. It is plainly furnished with two long, wooden tables flanked by benches.

The room is so plain that it is austere and looks unfinished. Apart from a simple carved frieze around the top of the wall, decorated with alternating symbols of Ulric and Sigmar, everything is undecorated plaster and wood. A successful Charm Test may convince a Sigmarite priest to confess — privately, and not within the hearing of any other priest — that the lavish decoration found in other buildings associated with Sigmar’s worship has been neglected because the Sigmarites do not want to give the Ulricans any cause to echo the common northern sentiment that Reiklanders are all soft southern fops.

An Ulrican priest, asked the same question, will reveal (again, privately) that the priests of the White Wolf are more than usually ascetic here, because they feel the need to represent northern toughness in front of the Sigmarites.

The Dormitories

To either side of the main hall is a door marked, respectively, with the hammer of Sigmar and the wolf ’s-head of Ulric. Each door leads to a dormitory accommodating six priests. These rooms are slightly more relaxed in their décor: the Ulrican dormitory is plain but comfortable; the Sigmarite counterpart is decorated tastefully, but not too lavishly.

The Kitchen and Stores

At the back of the main hall is a simple kitchen and store-room where meals are prepared and foodstuffs are stored.

The Shrine.name: The Shrine
The Shrine.text:
As the Altdorf to Middenheim road winds through the forest between Kutenholz and the Forest Hearth Inn, there is a clear side-turning marked by a large, white boulder. The wolf ’s-head symbol of Ulric is carved on one side of the boulder; Sigmar’s hammer is carved on the other. Both carvings are defaced as though someone has swung at them several times with a hammer or mace.

Any Dwarf, or anyone who makes a successful Trade (Stonemason) Test, can tell that the damage is recent and no more than a week old. It looks like a regrettable sign of the times.

Half a mile down the turning is an open area of flattish rocky ground, just over an acre in extent. A simple yet elegant building stands in the middle of the clearing. It is larger than a normal wayside shrine, and not unlike the temples typically found in larger villages: about 40-ft long with small and clearly symbolic crenellations and a low tower at one end. A narrow river runs along one side of the clearing, and the dense forest continues beyond it. The priests’ house stands at the edge of the clearing next to the river, about 70 yd from the shrine itself. This well kept building is smaller, lower and more functional, with shuttered windows.

The Legend of Shining Rock

The shrine is built on the site where the god (either Ulric or Sigmar, depending on the faith of the source) had paused to rest after a battle against the forces of Chaos but was ambushed.

In both versions of the legend, the god was weaponless. In the Sigmarite myth, the battle took place before Sigmar received Ghal Maraz from Kurgan Ironbeard, and his sword had shattered against the armour of the last Champion of Chaos he killed. In the Ulrican version, the god had been fighting in wolf form, chasing down the minions of Chaos who had stolen his great axe Blitzbeil.

In both tales, the god picked up a strange, glittering rock to shield himself from his attackers. One of their blows shattered part of it into a long sharp shard and, using it as a sword, he killed five hundred of his enemies before they fled.

The legend is well-known, and any Character who makes an Easy (+40) Lore (Theology) Test will recall its broad outlines. Sigmarite Characters will have heard a version where their patron deity is the hero, and Ulricans will know a version that casts the wolf-god in the same role.

Everyone knows that two versions of the legend exist. Ulricans claim that their version is older, and that the tale was co-opted by Sigmarite Reiklanders after the first Emperor was deified. Sigmarite doctrine maintains that their version is the authentic one, but a few will concede that he might have had Ulric’s help in the battle — in the form of supernatural aid, though, and not in person.

Inside the Shrine

The interior of the shrine is dominated by a long, thin outcrop of pale rock, which glitters and glistens in the light of two dozen large lamps that hang from the ceiling. The lamps’ brass bodies are marked with the alternating signs of the wolf ’s head and the twin-tailed comet, and the imagery of Sigmar and Ulric alternates in a similar fashion throughout.

There are no pews or prayer-stools in the shrine: the floor is clean but completely bare. Any of the attending priests can explain that this is because the Sigmarite way is to stand or kneel on bare stone, so they did not require pews; the Ulricans, not wanting to appear softer or less devoted, also eschewed their customary use of pews.

At the far end of the shrine, the ceiling rises in an octagonal tower. Beneath the centre of the tower is the highest part of the rock outcrop, which stands about 3 ft above floor level. A sharp break indicates where, according to the legends of both faiths, the god snapped a piece off the outcrop to defend himself.

An impressive statue of Ulric, depicted holding a shard of rock, stands against the back wall . As in most of Ulric’s temples, an eternal flame burns in a circular stone fire-pit in front of the statue. On entering the shrine, the sound of the flame flickering is audible, whilst the smell of the fire lingers and the temperature drops significantly.

An altar to Sigmar stands in the south-eastern part of this area, positioned so that worshippers facing it are looking in the direction of Karaz-a-Karak, the Dwarven citadel where, it is believed, Sigmar went on his last journey as a mortal. This alignment is common in Sigmarite temples, especially older ones.

Interior walls separate the public area of the shrine from two robing rooms: one for Sigmarite priests; the other for Ulrican priests. Beneath each is a small underground treasury, reached by a steep stone staircase under a trapdoor, where offerings and valuable ritual equipment are kept.

The Priests.name: The Priests
The Priests.text:
As mentioned already, the Place of Shining Rock is attended by priests of two faiths, making it almost unique in the Empire. Father @UUID[Actor.duKcRY7UmhR3swxc]{Gregor Braun} leads the priests of Sigmar. High priest Wolf-born @UUID[Actor.S9ldSbUY7DwfHtUW]{Fernand Wagner} commands those of Ulric. The priests are divided into three shifts, each consisting of two priests from each faith: while one shift prays in the chapel, another sleeps, and the third keeps a lookout for trouble from the forest — detaching two members to cook and serve meals as necessary. The shifts change every eight hours — this way the shrine is attended day and night.

The Place of Shining Rock is seen as a hard posting, with few luxuries. Only the most devout from either faith volunteer to serve there, either to test their devotion or to uphold the One True Faith in the face of the other cult. Despite the rivalry, there is seldom any conflict between the two contingents. The shrine is so unique in the Empire’s religious fabric that any kind of bad behaviour would embarrass one cult in front of its arch-rival, and bring down the wrath of the cult’s leaders upon the offender.

@UUID[Actor.duKcRY7UmhR3swxc]{Gregor Braun}

@UUID[Actor.4Kl4lEvEK2gLocBo]{Silvie Unterfaut}

@UUID[Actor.S9ldSbUY7DwfHtUW]{Fernand Wagner}

@UUID[Actor.fDTf37MCOXU1FhVB]{Manfred Ulricson}

Return to Shining Rock

Having first met them on a barge headed towards Altdorf, it is likely that the head of their monastry, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus}, has perished. Indeed, one of the Brothers may even have joined him. The survivor, or hopefully survivors, are intent on preserving the reputation of the later head of their monastry, and so were shocked to discover that he had in his possessions a piece of relic at Shining Rock.

Discrete inqueries have demonstrated that @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.bUxA8zyayMarTXP7]{Father Marcus} had no right to the relic, and the implication that he may have damaged it in the course of stealing a shard is deeply troubling. They have resovled to keep this piece of information to themselves, and seek to return the shard to Shining Rock. If he is still alive, Father Marcus will have come to the conclusion that the shard must be returned as well.

Unfortunately, neighter have good reason to travel to Shining Rock — certainly not in an official capacity. They are desperete to see the Shard returned, and will engage the Characters to help them in doing so. Thoguh neither is wealthy — and stealing as cult funds would only make spiritual matters even worse — they can offer only a single gold crown as payment. However, they assure the Characters that the spiritual rewards, in stark contrast to the meagre worldly ones, will be immesureable.

Adventure Ideas.name: Adventure Ideas
Adventure Ideas.text:
In a time of conflict between the Empire’s two most powerful religions, the unique shrine at the Place of Shining Rock takes on an even greater significance. A wide range of people can be encountered here, and the highly-charged religious and political significance of the place means that almost any encounter can turn dangerous very quickly.

The One True Faith

In more peaceful times, the Place of Shining Rock is a symbol of peace and coexistence between the faiths of Sigmar and Ulric, with religious differences amounting to no more than good-natured banter. With the Empire on the brink of civil war, though, things are different.

A mob of fanatics invades the shrine, intent on slaughtering the priests of the rival faith and destroying all the statues, altars, and other signs of that faith’s existence. The mob might be Ulricans led by @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{Sons of Ulric} or even by @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.nzsWxG9db2fdGjZM.JournalEntryPage.0sKLAqTMd6KMG9zw]{Wolf-kin} or Sigmarites led by flagellants, warrior priests, or even witch hunters. Anyone who resists, regardless of the faith they profess, is decried by the mob’s leaders as a heretic or an apostate, and runs a significant risk of being torn to pieces. Anyone who fails to join in with loud and enthusiastic cries of devotion runs a risk themselves — only slightly less — of being punished for their lack of zeal by being beaten unconscious and having their possessions seized by the mob’s leaders.

Use the @UUID[Actor.xyTpRk92mTGA9QOh]{profile} found in Empire in Ruins to represent these fantastics. The mob’s leaders will be in the upper two levels of their careers, and will have Talents reflecting their fanaticism and ability to stir up a mob: @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.x8g3U68oi8XzWiYr]{Commanding Presence}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.aE3pyW20Orvdjzj0]{Hatred (the other faith)}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.RyxOZqcBNZ7Zw721]{Holy Hatred}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.oGbDwnLOn3isPJpO]{Impassioned Zeal}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.WCXnFSV4WOSmzzc4]{Inspiring}, and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.XU7D9CCmumuhqDUi]{Public Speaker} are all useful.

The Characters can respond to the appearance of a mob in various ways, depending on their skills and preferences. The situation could turn into a defence of the shrine and its clearing, with the Characters leading a motley force of priests, monks, and visiting pilgrims against the howling mob.

More cerebral parties might try to defuse tensions before things turn violent, making opposed Charm Tests with the mob’s leaders in the hope of calming things down —or just playing for time until help arrives in the form of a noble visitor and his escort whom the priests are expecting. This visitor might even be the @UUID[Actor.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist} himself, and his escort of templars will be sufficient to even the odds. Players who take this option should be prepared to roleplay their speeches and arguments, and you should apply modifiers to their Tests based on how eloquently they have spoken.

If everything goes horribly wrong and both the shrine and the Characters appear to be doomed, there is always the possibility of divine intervention. Everyone in the mob will be accumulating Sin Points with every action, and if their leaders try making Pray Tests they may well incur the @Table[wrath]{Wrath of the Gods}. More spectacular interventions, even at a shrine like this one, are not common in the Old World, and should be used with great restraint. If possible, they should look like accidents or chance happenings, but the Characters to whom they happen — especially if they are devout — should be left wondering whether the hand of a deity was involved.

To make a volatile situation even worse, a mob of fanatics from the opposing religion might arrive at the same time, or shortly thereafter.

Let there be Peace

More peaceful, but equally inconvenient, might be a wandering mob of peace-seeking pilgrims who have decided to stay at the Place of Shining Rock, praying continuously to both gods until they intervene and resolve the crisis. While their intentions are good, they quickly turn the clearing around the shrine into a muddy quagmire with insufficient sanitation and rampant disease. The notes on the camp in @UUID[JournalEntry.7w2yyQTWCPXye9DS]{Chapter 3, ‘Journey to Shining Rock’ } will be useful in this scenario.

These wandering idealists take over the shrine, politely but firmly refusing entry to the attending priests unless they adopt the agenda of round-the-clock prayer and song themselves. Anyone else who attempts to enter — be they penniless pilgrims or Elector Counts — suffer the same treatment. The cause of peace recognises no authority higher than their own self-imposed mission, and while they themselves are peaceful, impatient troops could quickly turn the scene into a bloodbath. The Characters will have to exercise restraint and diplomacy to prevent a massacre here — a massacre which, perhaps, has been intended all along by certain cultists who have infiltrated the group.

In Boca Lupo

A @UUID[Actor.wDdApBY2jNIsOrnx]{White Wolf} has recently been spotted near the Shrine, leaving almost everyone a touch nervous. Most see the wolf as more or less what it appears to be — a particularly large and likely dangerous wolf. Even the Ulricans are concerned, as while the White Wolf is sacred to Ulric and sometimes seen as protectors, they are more often aggressors, representatives of the harsher nature of the God of War, Winter and Wolves.

The slaying of such a beast is a religious experience in its own right, and a recent influx of hopeful young pilgrims has arrived hoping to win temporal fame and spiritual favour. In particular, an uncommon pilgrimage of Tilean worshippers of Ulric has arrived, desperete to slay the beast. Unfortunately for them, the creature has proven difficult to track and even more difficult to slay, and already a handful of hopeful hunters have vanished in the forests surrounding the shrine.

There are varying opinions as to what should be done. The Sigmarites would like the beast killed or driven off. A few of the Ulricans would like it left alone — they see it’s presence at the Shrine as either divine, or perhaps more cynically, as a good draw for pilgrims once word gets around.

Others would like to hunt it for themselves, and while long tradition says they should stalk the beast alone, most are not above paying for a little help — even more so once the disappearances start to mount. Of course, should a Character slay the beast then the honour and blessing of Ulric would fall upon them, along with the right to wear the pelt of a white wolf openly. An invitation to join a knightly order, especially the Order of the White Wolf, is certain to follow.-

@UUID[Actor.wDdApBY2jNIsOrnx]{Skarr - The White Wolf of Shining Rock}

Altdorf in Chaos.name: Altdorf in Chaos
Altdorf in Chaos.text:
Changing Times

@UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheeragetru} has had one eye upon Altdorf for an age, knowing by the twisted threads of fate that this festering monument to human hubris would be its place of glorious liberation. Sheeragetru would have it no other way, for it will bring great pleasure to remake the spiritual home of Sigmar, who imprisoned the daemon so long ago.

The maddening gaze of a Lord of Change has influenced the city down through the years, with many of Altdorf ’s more sensitive citizens feeling the presence of the daemon close by. In recent months this unsettling influence has moved from the dreams of artists and poets into physical reality, and as the 8th of Brauzeit draws closer the scale and frequency of unusual phenomena will only increase.

This chapter provides a selection of unusual events that players might experience during their time in Altdorf. Some are unsettling, some are informative, a few are quite dangerous, and a few simply bizarre. These events serve to underline the reality-shaking events that may come should the Characters fail, and can be deployed any time they are in the city.

These events may also be used anywhere the influence of Chaos might be felt, and several would make good jumping off points for other adventures.

The Prophecy.name: The Prophecy
The Prophecy.text:
By this stage in the campaign, it is clear that the Empire’s veneer of unity, order, and civilisation is starting to crack. Even so, there are plenty of people who still believe in the Empire and refuse to acknowledge that anything is wrong. They ignore the growing unrest, the worrying news from all parts of the Empire, and the stories of Ratmen and Chaos-worshippers, and go to considerable lengths to explain such things away as perfectly normal events blown out of proportion, or deride them as ‘falsities and fearmongering’ promulgated by treasonous sorts with their own ineffable and unworthy agenda. Some even cast doubt upon the sanity of anyone who fears for the Empire’s future.

The Empire’s street-corner prophets are increasing in number and their rhetoric is becoming more deranged with every passing day, which makes it easy for the skeptics to write off anyone else’s concerns. These individuals are especially common in Altdorf at present, where they are spreading an extensive prophecy.

Hearing the Prophecy

It is unlikely the Characters will ever hear the entire prophecy all at one time. Instead, they might hear a piece here and a piece there. With a little imagination, it is possible to find many different ways for the prophecy to haunt the Characters and play on their nerves.

  • Street-corner prophets may include part of the prophecy in their ravings, only to be hauled away by the authorities for causing a disturbance before they deliver more than a couple of lines.

  • Fragments may be daubed on walls, or found on scraps of torn parchment in the homes of suspects and cultists.

  • Garbled lines might haunt a Character’s troubled dreams.

  • An overheard conversation might include a few words, perhaps in a voice far different from the voices of the speakers.

  • A dying mutant might gasp out a few more before expiring, or they might echo strangely from the void as a slain Daemon returns to the Realm of Chaos.

  • The Characters happen upon a ragged figure squatting in the street. They drop a handful of bones on the ground, stare at them, scrawl some symbols in the dust, and repeat the process. As the Characters approach, their face twists in a spasm of horror as they launch themself at a Character of your choice. They clutch the Character by the shoulders and scream the prophecy into their face before running wildly off into the passing crowds.

  • In the midst of conducting a ritual, a priest might suddenly develop a glassy stare and intone a phrase or two in a voice of unnatural depth and resonance before collapsing. When the priest comes to their senses, they remember nothing other than feeling immensely cold.

Stranger Prophecies

Familiar Fortellings

‘I see Darkness Gathering as the Last House of Joy Falls — beware, for Shadows Over Bögenhafen stir! Then Beloved Morr, resplendent in Vestments of Green, stands astride Sigmar’s Great River. Yea, I see Death on the Reik and I despair! For then the Stained Hand guides the Once Mighty Lord, and this Power Behind the Throne curses us all. Lo, the Horned Rat then claims the Broken King atop his Throne of Lies, and the White Walls Fall, leaving our Empire in Ruins! Tremble in fear, ye mighty, for the End Times have come.’

The Characters remember this scene from their earliest visit to Altdorf during @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.IjGUv51IPhj79Wxt.JournalEntryPage.MN27O2tN0lSOkvgm]{Manic Street Preacher}. They may be surprised to hear the same words spoken again from different mouths; it is useful to remind them of this particular prophecy at this point, should it have spilled their minds.

Gideon’s Guile

'A man bearing a false name travels the Empire, and many welcome him who should not. A hand strikes in the darkness, purple-shadowed. A crown drips blood, red with gore. A castle falls, that fell generations ago. Rats gnaw, and steal, and pray to the moon. A man’s face is stolen many, many times. The wolf eats the hammer, and chokes on its prey. The beasts in the forest awake and are hungry. Those outside will come inside, and those within shall surely perish if they do. Yet there are those inside who aid those outside, and many enemies are within!’

The End Times

‘Trust not your neighbour, for he may not be your neighbour! Fear the stranger, for stranger things are coming! Take the hammer from the wolf’s jaws and repair the walls and roof, for the storm is coming! Hold the hammer fast, keep the wolf close, and fight the darkness together!

The Changer of the Ways doth sit upon the Imperial throne! The Enemy is Within!’

For Grognards: A Portent of Doom

Veterans of the first edition Enemy Within campaign may have heard a prophecy very much like this one when they visited Middenheim in Power Behind the Throne. In this version, a few details have been changed in the interests of consistency with the Director’s Cut version.

You can change some of these details back if it will entertain the Players — or, better yet, confuse and worry them. If you feel the Characters have influenced things sufficiently, try to choose some words that reflect their own past choices and achievements. In particular, if they are wrestling with any particular issue, who to support for the claim to the Imperial Throne, the fate of Ghal Maraz and so on, try to pepper in some appropriately vague pronouncements.

Here are a few substitute (or additional) lines that refer to the first-edition campaign:

‘I see a great withering and putrefaction to the north, its miasma blowing down on the north wind to choke us all. Truly, Something is Rotten in Kislev!’

‘I see fire and slaughter sweeping the land! I see cities burning, and rivers afire! I see the Empire in Flames!’

‘I see graves yawning wide, and corpses marching! The Restless Dead shall enlighten us!’

Players who experienced the third-edition Enemy Within campaign might be treated to the following additional lines:

‘Beneath a black cowl are three faces, and no one knows the truth!’

‘Soldier, wizard, noble, hood — who is bad and who is good?’ (this doggerel couplet might be effective if the Characters hear group of children chanting it in the course of some game)

‘The Enemy Below dims the sun! The beasts are loosed, and all is confusion!’

‘All march against the Enemy Without, but the city shall fall at the sound of a bell!’

‘Let the Hammer strike the Bell before the Bell strikes the hour, or Altdorf is lost!’

‘The Enemy Within is the Enemy Beyond, and madness shall bring victory!’

Wilder Magic.name: Wilder Magic
Wilder Magic.text:
Magic and Chaos are closely intertwined — indeed, some go so far as to claim that they are identical. Be that as it may, magic can behave in unexpected ways when a spellcaster is in close proximity to a potent source of Chaos. While in Altdorf, or in any of the other nine locations that fall under the eye of Tzeentch after Ghal Maraz has been retrieved, you may substitute the @Table[wild-magic] table for the Miscast Tables in the WFRP rulebook.

All of this exciting and particularly mutable magical activity has not gone unnoticed. As well as terrifying wizards throughout the city, a pair of daemons have been drawn to Altdorf as gibbering moths to a flame.

The Blue Scribes of Tzeentch

These Daemons look very much like Blue Horrors, but are much more intelligent and powerful. It is said that Tzeentch created the two Daemons personally, named them P’tarix and Xirat’p, and tasked them with learning every spell in existence.

The Blue Scribes ride a Disc of Tzeentch through realms mortal and eternal, P’tarix scrawling frantically with a quill crafted from a Lord of Change’s pin-feather while Xirat’p reads the written words to check for mistakes, and in doing so, unleashing the spell’s power on any creature unfortunate enough to be nearby. The Characters, and especially any wizards, may notice them skulking about the city. This causes a great terror in any who witness them, but unusually most seem to forget about the horrors as soon as they are out of sight.

If left alone, they ignore mortals and, provided they are not studying spells when encountered, they are not especially dangerous. If they are threatened, Xirat’p starts reading at random from the accumulated scrolls, casting a random spell each round.

No profile is provided here, as the pair are inteded to reflect the magical chaos of Altdorf (and annoy any spell casters) rather than attack the Characters outright. However, if required you may treat the pair as Blue Horrors, with a shared Trait of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.EO05HX7jql0g605A]{Fly (60)}, and the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.yc1z6Jq6fTlWjNKH]{Random Caster} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.cT6rnVaMMgS1OC2o]{Spell Syphon} Traits as shown below. For more on the Blue Scribes see Winds of Magic.

@Table[wild-magic]

A Touch of Chaos.name: A Touch of Chaos
A Touch of Chaos.text:
There are few events as immediately indicative of the presence of Chaotic influence that then the manifestation of Daemons on a city street. As the day of reckoning draws closer this very thing happens with increasing frequency. Event as Colleges of Magic rush to investigate, more subtle works of Chaos exert their influence on the citizens of Altdorf.

The Body Thief

As the Characters pass by, a townsperson or other minor NPC falls to the ground, clutching their head and screaming in agony. The thrashing body is hard to examine (–20 penalty to all related Tests), but shows no signs of any wounds or disease — until [[/br 1d10]] rounds later, when the unfortunate’s skin begins to split and peel back. A Daemon is struggling to free itself from the possessed body as if from a straitjacket. Roll on the following table to determine the nature of the Daemon:

@Table[body-thief]

Everyone seeing the horrible process must make a Fear Test based on the Daemon’s Fear rating.

The Daemon must make an Extended Agility Test (5 SLs) to free itself from its fleshy prison. Each remaining SL counts as one @Condition[Entangled] Condition. Once it is free, the Daemon attacks the nearest mortal creature.

Marsie Wagnershoff Child of Chaos

@UUID[Actor.tC4Etbl7Br01ayVB]{Marsie} is a baker’s daughter from @UUID[JournalEntry.ZeJj1Sg9PGwUgCbj.JournalEntryPage.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv]{Diesdorf}, and has been in Altdorf for a few weeks now, having come seeking to better her lot. Things have not gone at all according to plan. Her mutation only struck in the last few days, but it has since quite understandably consumed her entire life. An horrific experience, her brain now gives spontaneous rise to a swarm of maggotty worms. They have eaten their way through her skull from the inside, devouring her hair, and have since squirmed ceaselessly about her scalp.

She has brushed, washed, and scraped them away, but always they return within minutes, painfully burrowing out from her skin. @UUID[Actor.tC4Etbl7Br01ayVB]{Marsie} is otherwise an innocent soul, and only wants to somehow survive and escape the city. She hopes to find a cure for her condition amongst the wise Hedgefolk of the countryside.

@UUID[Actor.tC4Etbl7Br01ayVB]{Marsie} does not answer questions. If conscious, she is interested only in escape and uses her powers freely to get away. This includes pushing people in the streets into @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.DrNUTPeodEgpWTnT]{Frenzy} to distract pursuers. If the characters capture the woman and render her unconscious, they still have an unconscious mutant to deal with. Even the Shallyans baulk at such a wretch, and the creature’s power would be very useful to cultists in the city and mutant raiders in the forests.

The Characters might find themselves with few ideas beyond killing Marsie, but this should not sit well. If they do resort to slaying her, they displease merciful Shallya and accumulate Sin points accordingly. If they find some way of neutralising her power and removing its mutations, Shallya may reward those who did with a Fate point each.

Flamers of Tzeentch.name: Flamers of Tzeentch
Flamers of Tzeentch.text:
Flamers of Tzeentch are odd creatures, proof if it were needed that the Changer of Ways is capable of truly bizarre creations. More akin to an ambulatory fungus than any mortal creature, the Flamers of Tzeentch propel themselves by emitting bilious gouts of gas from multitudinous, ever shifting orifices.

@UUID[Actor.U4fQhVCwwSnsXgpu]{Flamers Of Tzeentch}

Despite their unwieldy appearance they are capable of bursts of rapid movement, and those who have had cause to do battle with them are thankful the things are less common than the pink and blue Horrors that seem a favoured daemon of Tzeentch.

Though the creatures bulk is not inconsiderable, their main form of attack is the emission of great gouts of many hued flame. This is not fire in the traditional sense, but instead an intense warpfire, the raw stuff of Chaos itself. It is a fickle power, often benefitting the targets, but it brings with it the warping curse of corruption, and so Tzeentch is pleased with it in any case.

A Flamer of Tzeentch would be a terrible thing indeed to appear in Altdorf, a singular sign that these are strange days indeed. All who seen it would be questioned intently, and any touched by its flames would be suspect.

Events and Encounters.name: Events and Encounters
Events and Encounters.text:
The influence of a Lord of Change is affecting the minds of Altdorfers as well as their physical surroundings. Here are some ideas for events and encounters — they may become more extreme as time goes on.

Restless Locals

Even before things begin to happen that defy the laws of nature and common sense, the minds of the townsfolk are opening to the potential for change. Ambitions and resentments are more keenly felt, and agitators stir the populace to unrest and even to violence. Riots break out in the streets, for any reason or for no apparent reason at all, with mobs marching in various parts of the city, attacking anyone who gets in their way and sometimes looting the premises along their route.

These mobs are lead by individuals who have fallen under the sway of Tzeentch, and find themselves drawn to the Characters. While the mob at large might be reasoned with, the @UUID[Actor.QDC5cDPANpLndmlW]{Agitators} who lead them are much more difficult to intimidate.

Frenzied Altdorfers

The Characters are passing through one of Altdorf ’s many markets when a shopper suddenly seizes a leg of mutton as an improvised weapon and launches into a frothing attack. There is no warning: the Characters cannot avoid being @Condition[Surprised].

On every subsequent round, another ordinary citizen joins in the murderous frenzy. While in theory the Characters could be overwhelmed, in practice they are almost certain to incapacitate the attackers as quickly as they are created.

The @UUID[Actor.KUNfs5bRCLNCaDjB]{Frenzied townsfolk} and servants have little chance of doing any damage to the veteran Characters. The main problem is that these people are just ordinary city folk, and cutting them down like Daemons is not something that heroic adventurers should be doing.

While the Characters may assume that the first attacker was simply hiding their rage, make sure that, in the next round, they see a young citizen who had already started to flee the scene stop, turn with a murderous look in their eyes, and leap to the attack. Characters who make Challenging (+0) Perception Tests in subsequent rounds see the same thing happen again, and again, and again. The Characters should realise that something is driving the honest citizens of Altdorf into a murderous frenzy.

The Frenzy automatically expires if an attacker drops to 1 or fewer Wounds. Reason suddenly returns, and, if they can still move, they try to flee. The Characters may also notice this.

Smart Characters may start looking for the cause of this trouble. This requires a Hard (–20) Perception Test. If it succeeds, the Character spots a figure passing close to two citizens just as they enter Frenzy. She is wearing nondescript clothes and a deep hood covers her head. The woman does not realise that she has been spotted until the Characters make a move. If they succeed in grabbing her, they can see the reason for the hood: the woman has worms in place of hair. Any Character touching her in a round when she is conscious and takes no other action is targeted by her @UUID[Actor.tC4Etbl7Br01ayVB.Item.IHCWHrxpupUwRX2Z]{Induce Frenzy} power. The woman starts with whichever Character is holding her.

Unstable Foundations

The Characters are passing by a house or a small shop that clearly belongs to a wizard. Exactly what makes this clear is up to you: the house may have a sign hanging outside that advertises magical services, it may belong to an NPC wizard with whom they have become acquainted, or it may be ringed around with mystical symbols carved or painted on the walls, for example.

As the Characters come close to the building, its outline begins to waver. It becomes translucent, then transparent, and within a few seconds there is an audible pop as it passes through a rift in reality and into the Realm of Chaos. While the rift only exists for a second or two, and one who looks directly at it must make a @Terror[4]{Terror 4} Test because of the things they see within.

A successful Challenging (+0) Lore (Chaos or Magic) Test suggests that the building became magically unstable, and was sucked into the Realm of Chaos as a result. But surely, that only happens to Daemons…

Signs of the Times

Like any settlement of any size, Altdorf is full of signs. Not all townsfolk can read, so a sign with an image of the goods a shop sells, or of an inn’s name, is far more useful than a written name. In times such as these, though, the letters might be preferable, since images have a tendency to come to life.

A chicken on a weathervane might flutter down to cause havoc in the streets, for example. A dragon might pull itself out of an inn sign to spread fiery panic, or a statue might climb down from its plinth and lay about itself with stony weapons. The possibilities are endless.

The creatures might stay the same size as their painted or sculpted originals, or they might grow (or shrink, as appropriate) to their natural size. Their profiles are the same as for the original creatures, with the following adjustments:

Characteristics: Intelligence, Willpower, and Fellowship are all 0.

Traits: Add @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.UB4mDroL6S1F9B4u]{Construct}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.xsGbDFqK2qh7lsIj]{Corruption (Minor)}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.3wCtgMDNnu8MFmyk]{Immunity (Criticals)}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.IAWyzDfC286a9MPz]{Immunity to Psychology}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.D0ImWEIMSDgElsnl]{Unstable}. Animated statues add @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.VUJUZVN3VYhOaPjj]{Armour 3 (metal)} or @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.VUJUZVN3VYhOaPjj]{Armour 4 (stone)}.

Hit and Run

A coach comes rattling down the street with no horses pulling it. It runs down anyone in its path, which counts as a Charge and Stomp from an Enormous creature. It can only be stopped by a successful Very Hard (–30) Strength Test which achieves 5 SLs in a single round. Up to six Characters can cooperate on the test (see @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.lQThXbnpgQ30VBXR#assistance]{Assistance}).

In addition to its Stomp attack, the coach lashes out with its two poles. Each one counts as a club (Hand Weapon) with Long Reach and SB + 6 damage. The Enemy in Shadows Companion includes hit locations for coaches and other vehicles.

@UUID[Actor.yA2ORx3iuGfAKMzX]{Animated Coach}

Moving Day

Amid a great commotion, a stream of animated furniture comes running down the street, chased by its uncomprehending but determined owner. Long legged side-tables run like deer; chairs run or waddle depending on their construction; a bed tramples its way through the throng like a charging bull; and all around scamper low side-tables, footstools, and other small items. If not stopped, the furniture will throw itself into the Reik and swim for the far bank, seeking to return to the forest where its wood once grew as trees. Someone skilled in the Jade Wind may be able to use Charm Animal to calm the frolicking furniture, but otherwise they careen freely through the streets.

This is obviously rather surreal, and you may play this scene for laughs if you wish. Of course, to the denizens of Altdorf it is anything but funny. Unnatural occurances are rarely benign and, even should the furniture make it out of the city, those who previously owned the fitful furnishings are likely to face investigation as potential witches themselves. If you wish to play the scene more for horror than hearty laughs, have a four poster bed trample some guards to a bloody pulp on its way to the river, or some floating drapery strangle a bright wizard who attempted to set it aflame. Remember that it is quite possible to leave the Players in fits of laughter while threatening the very lives of their Characters.

You can decide how many pieces of furniture are involved in this bizarre incident, and of what types. Profiles below are for large, medium, and small pieces.

@UUID[Actor.g6iMzs4OsqeW2hs4]{Animated Furniture, Large}

@UUID[Actor.ZLRDoZmP0bOlvEVw]{Animated Furniture, Medium}

@UUID[Actor.EUpaOhyGuIaWP26j]{Animated Furniture, Small}

Dish of the Day

The Characters are passing by a butcher’s shop or stall when some of its carcasses become infused with unholy life, writhing off their hooks and platters to attack the nearest living creatures. They are somewhat hampered by having been skinned and partially butchered, but they are capable of putting up a considerable fight nonetheless.

@UUID[Actor.O61CWMK0vYfvB1C9]{Cow Carcass}

@UUID[Actor.FWikZu04UmX8lP4B]{Sheep Carcass}

@UUID[Actor.sAePF8SGiX2cotmj]{Pig Carcass}

Unnatural Weather

As far back as history records, strange weather events have been associated with evil portents. The Enemy in Shadows Companion includes a simple system for handling weather, but given the increasingly Chaotic nature of events in Altdorf, you could also decide to change the weather however you want, whenever you want, especially if the Players are slowing down and need a new challenge to galvanise them. You might roll some dice just for effect, or you might simply announce that the weather change has happened.

In order to keep things controllable, it is recommended that a Chaotic weather effect is fairly localised: no more than, say, 100 yards across. But if you’re up to the challenge of having it affect the whole city, feel free!

Here are some suggestions for Chaotic weather effects, but feel free to use your imagination and invent more. Remember what the Characters have been through on the earlier parts of the campaign: if they find themselves pelted with something that stirs a memory or strikes a chord — whether it be sausages or kittens — the experience will be all the more memorable!

Rain: Frogs, fish, blood, pus, beer.

Hail: Pebbles, teeth, hazelnuts, pennies, diamonds, Warpstone.

Fog: Incense, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.wgFj3lFhCuO8OeDb]{Moonflower} vapours, liquefied @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.jTFOrokjEHbi12rT]{Ranald’s Delight}, sleeping gas (Challenging (+0) Endurance Test or gain @Condition[Unconscious] Condition).

Thunder: Laughter, a line from @UUID[.RSbwA0azjJla0HBq]{the prophecy}, screams, clashing weapons, animal sounds, music.

Lightning: Turns anything it strikes to ice, stone, or some other substance, mimics a spell effect, @UUID[Actor.iDy8SDTwJSlCzZMl]{Pink Horrors} or other small Daemons appear where it strikes.

A Spy on the Road.name: A Spy on the Road
A Spy on the Road.text:
The journey from @UUID[JournalEntry.fgrD3J7lhVYdc7VF.JournalEntryPage.Ip4gsNUFocBJQGmk#castle-reikguard]{Castle Reikguard} back to Altdorf is straightforward, and relatively quick on horseback. The Characters ought to be at least a day ahead of the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} unless they used up all their spare time at Castle Reikguard.

There is a sense of peace throughout the Reikland. News of the upcoming wedding is spreading throughout the province and provides common folk with a great sense of relief. On their journey, if the Characters mention they are on their way to the capital, people might ask if they are attending the wedding and, if so, can they pass on good wishes. Only the most maladjusted of churls would opine that the Princess is too low born and Ulrican to be marrying the Crown Prince.

During the journey the Characters should have several opportunities to spot that they are being followed at a distance by a Halfling on a pony. This is Hugo Bottomdown, a rather incompetent spy in the employment of Etelka Toppenheimer of Sudenland. She has ordered Hugo to keep an eye on @UUID[JournalEntry.fgrD3J7lhVYdc7VF.JournalEntryPage.Ip4gsNUFocBJQGmk#castle-reikguard]{Castle Reikguard}, and he is fixated on the Characters.

If Hugo notices that he has been spotted, he guides his horse into the undergrowth by the side of the road to escape notice. However, once he thinks the coast is clear, he will ride hard to catch up with the Characters and continue to shadow them.

If Hugo is cornered, he becomes indignant.

‘Very well, I may have been keeping tabs on you. I act in the interests of a noble elector of our great Empire, and you must let me work unhindered! Now, I will be kind enough to assume that you are not up to anything untoward. You go your way, and I shall go mine.’

If the Characters let Hugo go, he resumes following them after an hour. If he is threatened, he proves surprisingly dedicated to his role, fights with fierce bravery, and even carries a small vial of poison with which to end his own life if he is captured. He never reveals which elector hired him.

Hugo carries a note from his employer on him, which he may either drop, if the Characters do not search him; or have upon his person if they do. Whilst the handout may provide some clues that Hugo was commissioned by someone in Sudenland (Pfeildorf is the capital, and Solland an older and grander province that Toppenheimer hopes to emulate) the true import of this information becomes apparent later.

The Handout reads:

A New Dawn for Solland

Actions required as vital priorities in the service of her majesty:

  1. Acquire horse, camping gear, trail rations, spare uniforms.

  2. At Pfiefdorf ask for Fione the Thresher. Give her the uniforms and pay her. The word is Heideinheim.

  3. Travel to the Reikland. Confirm the marriage between the Todbringers and the House of the Third Wilhelm. Record any persons of interest.

  4. Report back before the solstice.

The Return to Altdorf

The Characters may be shocked to see so many soldiers camped outside Altdorf. At first they might even think the city may be under siege. Fortunately, it becomes clear that these troops are gathered to partake in a great parade to mark the wedding.

The Characters can make their way to Helstein Manor in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.cDOlXEpTvnuaOJ0P.JournalEntryPage.7vI2gXjiyjfMdzDW]{Mauerblumchen}. For political reasons the Todbringers do not keep their own estate in Altdorf, but stay at the lavish townhouse of their loyal subjects, the noble Helsteins of Middenheim. @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric}, @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim}, and the Todbringers are all here.

@UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} debriefs the Characters, as the other members of the household are busy with the wedding preparations. He reviews their questions to the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} and gently cajoles them if they forgot to ask an obvious question.

Wilhelmina Novak (of the Withering Eye), Wulfrum Ahlquist (of the Public Eye), and Gislind Ursin (of the Hollow Eye) are all in Altdorf at this time, preparing lessons for the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.EmhvOkkzAir6pzCB.JournalEntryPage.OiAVm63T9JEFsVfR]{University of Altdorf}. Should the Characters wish to track them down they can do so. The three tutors dress in the same grey robes as their comrades at the castle.

Though formidable, the tutors are socially awkward. They are more comfortable behind a podium than mixing with other academics, or holding forth in front of awed (or bored) students.

If the Characters want to do away with them quietly, this is not hard. But the trio never reveal anything about their background or motives — no matter how carefully they are questioned.

The Parade.name: The Parade
The Parade.text:
The impending nuptials deserve a public display of celebration and what better way to signal a great alliance than a military parade to showcase the might of the Empire united? Such an occasion demands an audience of the most exalted individuals in Sigmar’s Realm, those who wield such power that nations could crumble before their armies.

No less than three Elector Counts (Reikland, Middenheim, and Nuln) and two Cult Electors (Sigmar and Ulric) attend this great event.

The Characters are also invited. @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina} and @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Heinrich Todbringer} secured them an invitation, knowing they are useful observers, and able to handle any difficult situations which might arise. This is a great display of shared military might with countless standards, drums, and blaring horns marching across the artillery fields outside the city walls.

The sun is shining and there is just enough wind to keep banners flying. In the midst of all this pomp and ceremony, there are notable absences — the wizards have declined to participate, there are no mercenaries, and the Emperor knows better than to insist Elves or Dwarfs join such a display.

The parade starts at 2:00 p.m and continues until 7:30 p.m.

The Pavilion

The Royal spectators watch the parade from a newly raised pavilion. The arms of the Reikland, Middenheim, and Nuln fly from the tent, to reflect the presence of three Elector Counts. There is a large crowd of Altdorfers kept safely away from the pavilion, corralled behind a wooden barrier. The guests sit around three sides of a long table with a fine view of the parade ground, but events in the tent are more diverting than the display. Most make a cursory effort to watch the proceedings, but often move seats and stand to talk in small groups. Servants continually refresh the table with a supply of victuals and wines.

Mixing in the Highest Society

The party knows the Middenheim court and the Graf, so they are used to socialising with the nobility. But never before have they been part of a small gathering which apparently includes the Emperor, another Elector Count, and many powerful courtiers. The party has the opportunity to observe these exalted individuals and, if they are tactful and follow the correct protocol, perhaps even talk with them.

The Characters cannot approach the Emperor’s double directly. If any Character wants to speak with him, they need a high-ranking go-between (such as the @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf}, @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug}, or @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle}) to vouch for them. Alternatively, @UUID[Actor.bLxn6nG74TUEQmiS]{von Fielbach} (who is playing ‘Emperor’) may request their company for a moment. He largely avoids socialising to avoid close scrutiny. @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} is more accessible. She is curious about the current dispositions of Middenheim and Reikland, so she may speak directly to the Characters — if she thinks they know something or seem amusing. Should they wish to approach the countess, her high steward permits them.

Didn't we Meet at the Opera?

If the Party has played @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-rnhd.journals.SsYATFVcPahLsAHN]{‘A Night at the Opera’ }, they may have met the countess. If they made a good impression, she greets them with condescending approval. Otherwise, she’ll pretend to have forgotten them in their entirety.

They see a different side to the countess here. Despite her reputation, she is an adept politician, who makes astute observations about the situation. She uses her observations to her advantage.

The other notables can be approached directly — the Characters wouldn’t be here if they were people of no consequence. The PCs do need a good opening to address such important people in conversation. Needless to say, the Characters are expected to dress in their finest. Anyone in the tent with a military standing wears dress uniform, but not armour. @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} has an especially fine tunic that is somehow both formal and the height of fashion.

Whose Side Are You On?

The Characters’ behaviour here influences their reputation as supporters of the Sigmarite or Ulrican faction. If they lend vocal support to one party over the other, they change their allegiance score.

Remember: this is about reputation, not reality. During the event, keep track of each time the Characters act in favour of moderate or partisan Sigmarites and Ulricans. At the end, take a view of where they ended up and change their score by somewhere between –2 and +2 accordingly.

The Emperor's Party

The ‘Emperor’ (@UUID[Actor.bLxn6nG74TUEQmiS]{von Fielbach}) — is here to present the Middenheimers a healthy, vigourous ‘Karl Franz’. He remains quiet and distant from the proceedings to avoid close scrutiny, aided by two High Helm knights, a cadre within the Reiksguard. Moderate Sigmarite.

Grand Theogonist @UUID[Actor.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Yorri XV} — accompanied by two Knights Griffon, the Grand Theogonist is dressed in full priestly regalia. He is keen to smooth the discord with the Ulricans. After all, the marriage should place them tactfully under the wing of the Reikland. This occasion should placate the Middenheimers. Moderate Sigmarite.

High Capitular @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar} — a less compromising priest than Yorri, Volkmar is not here to show weakness to the Cult of Ulric, or make any concessions. He doesn’t do small talk. Partisan Sigmarite.

Graf @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Liepmund Holzkrug} — the High Lord Ambassador puts on the charm, particularly for @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle}, @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris}, and Ambassador @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.rSRadYoaNXkEq8gs.JournalEntryPage.IedMJf8kVeLmn63R#lady-of-the-commandery-yabo-chao,-weijins-venerable-ambassador]{Yabo Chao}. He scrutinises the important guests for weaknesses which he, or his spies, might exploit in future. Moderate Sigmarite.

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Yann Zuntermein} — the head of the Altdorf Ordo Terriblis is here with @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug} as a member of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.W4LFOIduFZoqSNsN.JournalEntryPage.e1vvDKWEn2EYw0gZ]{Black Chamber’s} Inner Circle. He observes and sows discord between the various parties in attendance. Moderate Sigmarite in appearance.

Grey Guardian @UUID[Actor.1Fw8roY9zezj0jAn]{Immanuel-Ferrand Holswig-Schliestein }— the High Chancellor proposed this parade to demonstrate Reikland’s military might. He argues in favour of centralising the Empire, stopping short of anything which causes obvious offence. Partisan Sigmarite.

The Middenheim Delegation

Graf @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Boris Todbringer} — the Graf is not happy to give away @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{his daughter}, but he’s persuaded that peace in the Empire should take precedence. He maintains a polite distance from the Emperor’s party and broods on the price he is paying. Moderate Ulrican.

@UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim} — the preceptor of the Knights Panther is in good spirits and, at first, thoroughly enjoys the parade. As he realises the power of the Reikland forces, he becomes perturbed and makes sarcastic comments about the Altdorf regiments. Moderate Ulrican.

@UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric Valgeir} — the High Priest does not like Altdorf and is unimpressed by ‘preening southerners marching about in fancy frills’. He sticks with the Ulricans but keeps his opinions largely to himself, bar the occasional growl. Partisan Ulrican

@UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina Todbringer} — the ‘Princess’ is resigned to her situation. This is a dull occasion to be endured, but she’s curious to know what agendas are at play in the pavilion. She asks the characters to make enquiries if they hold back. Moderate Ulrican.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.actors.ZyMHHLG9tNTDIw8S]{Hildegarde Zimperlich} — the chaperone knows her place and will go with the Graf ’s wishes, even though she whole-heartedly disapproves of her ward marrying a Reiklander. This doesn’t stop her making critical comments about everything in sight. Moderate Ulrican.

Lord @UUID[Actor.BmkwksUQBFGJr48x]{Malthe Barthelm} — a young Nordlander whose father, Harman Barthelm, is a commander in the Nordland State Army. Malthe is out of his depth, but quietly plays his role as loyal vassal of the @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf}. He’s secretly a Nordland separatist and plans to assassinate @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina} at the wedding tomorrow. Moderate Ulrican in appearance, Partisan Sigmarite in reality.

Others

Countess @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle von Liebwitz} — a sharp-witted political player. Emmanuelle is here to advance her aim to take over Sudenland. She is accompanied by High Steward Hildemar Kalb and Moritz Arbogast, a Knight of the Blazing Sun. Moritz was chosen deliberately as he is neither a Sigmarite nor an Ulrican. Moderate Sigmarite.

@UUID[Actor.6eNwY93t5wjxPYOs]{Colonel Sievers} — the frontier commander is in Altdorf trying to raise an army to attack the Orcs massing in the Badlands. He is uncomfortable in this refined setting and has no luck persuading Karl-Franz of the threat. Moderate Sigmarite.

There are several dozen guards, servants, and officious factotums busying themselves with security and catering to the whims of the guests.

Plots at the Parade.name: Plots at the Parade
Plots at the Parade.text:
During the parade, several parties are working to their own agenda.

Plot 1 - The Double

The Emperor’s double is here to give the impression Karl-Franz is in sound mind and body, ready for the joyous alliance of two of the Empire’s greatest families. Unfortunately for him, this is the first time he’s been faced with @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle} and @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Boris}, who may see through the sham and take offence. The Characters could discover this isn’t the real Emperor — and perhaps wonder why Karl-Franz is absent.

Plot 2 - Fuel to the Fire

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} sees the parade as the perfect opportunity to stir the pot and advance the likelihood of civil war. He is subtle, but works carefully to stoke hostility between factions. The Characters could sense that Zuntermein is manipulating the situation and suspect his motives.

Plot 3 - I Just Need an Army

@UUID[Actor.6eNwY93t5wjxPYOs]{Colonel Sievers} was invited to the parade as a trusted subordinate to the Emperor. He hopes to use this opportunity to persuade Karl-Franz to take swift action against the Orcs in the Badlands.

But the Colonel is a fish out of water, more comfortable stalking Greenskins in the mountains than negotiating politics in the capital. The Characters become acquainted with Sievers and possibly help him talk with the ‘Emperor’.

Plot 4 - Political Leverage

Countess @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle von Liebewitz} seeks political advantage and to negotiate support for her claim to Sudenland. She wishes to talk with @UUID[Actor.1Fw8roY9zezj0jAn]{Immanuel-Ferrand Holswig-Schliestein}, assuming his support for the annexation of Ubersreik makes him a likely ally. She plans to use the false Emperor as leverage. The Characters could help Emmanuelle and gain her gratitude or just learn more about the situation in the south.

Plot 5 - Porcine Pranks

This gathering of the exalted ruling classes is a perfect opportunity for a priestess of Ranald to cause mischief. Petra Schneller has painted three large sows in the colours of Altdorf (blue and red), Middenheim (blue and white), and Nuln (black with a crude yellow lion). She’s given them ale and a dose of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.jTFOrokjEHbi12rT]{Ranald’s Delight}. The plan is to unleash them in the pavilion at an opportune moment. The Characters can deal with the mayhem and impress everyone with their hog-handling prowess.

Events.name: Events
Events.text:
The Marching Formations

Although much of the military parade is a backdrop to the intrigue and events in the pavilion, it’s important the Characters know what’s happening on the field. Whilst this is ostensibly a display of combined Reikland and Middenheim forces, the latter had few regiments in marching distance of the city when the order was despatched — and they are sorely (and intentionally) under-represented. Each regiment carries its banner and all salute the pavilion as they pass.

TimeEvent
2:00-2:20p.m.The High Command - @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.YA2Wi0B3FBO4qMGS]{Reiksmarshall Kurt Helborg} leads the parade, holding aloft his Runefang at the head of the command section. Accompanying him are mounted standard bearers carrying the colours of the Emperor, the Reikland, Middenheim, Graf Todbringer, Altdorf, Countess von Liebwitz, and Nuln, in that order. Several heralds blow fanfare trumpets and march proudly alongside.
2:20–2:40p.m.

Knightly Orders and Pistolkorps - The Reiksguard lead, with the Inner Circle to the fore, followed by preceptors and several ‘banners’ of knights, their steel armour glinting brightly in the sun. A regiment of Knights Panther follow, including many from the Middenheim chapter. The Knights of the Blazing Sun have sent sufficient knights to serve their duty to the Emperor and no more.

Three regiments of pistoliers follow, drawn from Nuln, Middenheim, and the Reikland. Several Reiklanders fire into the air, startling the Middenheim horses, but the riders bring them under control.

2:40–3:30 p.m.

Regiments of Foot - The Carroburg Greatswords lead the infantry, carrying their zweihanders over their shoulders. They fly their own banner and the ‘wedding gift’ from Middenheim (assuming the Characters gave it to the Crown Prince).

Teutogen Guard — Ar-Ulric’s personal bodyguards glower at the crowd as they pass. They salute with the Ulrican sign of the wolf.

Nuln Greatswords — The Countess’ personal honour guards accompanied her to Altdorf. She winks at them as they pass.

Imperial Palace Guard, foot knights of the Reiksguard, including a band of High Helms.

3:30–4:10p.m.State Regiments - A full battalion of Altdorf Halberds from @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.cDOlXEpTvnuaOJ0P.JournalEntryPage.Sk2zs5EOYGYzywSq]{Hammerpfad’s} barracks, led by the famous Company of Honour with Captain Otto Helstein leading. Several companies of Reikland Halberds follow. Keen observers see notable absences, thanks to the force occupying Ubersreik. Middenheim is represented only by the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.9GDZ8Z1EReHLFc6i]{Swords of Ulric}, who march with heads held high and no attempt to keep a tight formation.
4:10–5:00p.m.

Artillery - A loud clanking heralds the arrival of the Steam Tank Conqueror with an Imperial engineer standing in the hatch. The crowd cheers with enthusiasm. A battery of Great Cannon follow, pulled on limbers by strong dray horses and accompanied by their crews.

A motley collection of Helblaster Volley Guns, Helstorm Rocket Batteries, and several other experimental weapons — A small company of Imperial engineers accompany them, looking almost as eccentric as their inventions. Another Steam Tank follows, The Indomitable. It has problems with its steering and causes a serious incident (see @UUID[.CMbWSTuTuhbZtid4#4:40-p.m.]{4:40 p.m}).

A regiment of Imperial Outriders trot after the mayhem caused by the Steam Tank. Another battery of Great Cannon follow and halt for their well-drilled crews to swiftly unlimber the guns ready for the artillery demonstration.

5:00–5:45p.m.Artillery demonstration - The first shot scatters every bird within 2 miles.
5:45–6:15p.m.

Regiments of Foot - Several companies of Handgunners from Altdorf and the Reikland. Their guns are polished to an impressive shine.

They are followed by regiments of Crossbowmen, with just one Middenheim contingent amongst the sea of Altdorf and Reikland livery.

Altdorf Spears march past, a little less disciplined than their fellow soldiers. Some wave to relatives and friends in the crowd.

The Fighting Cocks are a company of Halflings attached to the Altdorf garrison. They were especially keen to join the parade. They waddle along in loose formation, beaming with pride.

6:15–6:30p.m.Respite - A brief pause in proceedings while stewards lay out the ‘battleground’ for the mock battle.
6:30–7:00p.m.Mock battle - A staged event with Altdorf and Middenheim swordsmen sparring in mock combat as a demonstration of fighting prowess. It starts out rather tame, but later escalates.  
7:00–7:20p.m.Closing Parade - The Knights Griffon are led by Grandmaster Bacham, who has taken umbrage at their place in the parade. The parade ends with another company of Reiksguard, the last of which carries the Emperor’s colours once again.

As the following incidents unfold in the pavilion, the Players need to choose what to do — they can strike up conversations, involve themselves in what happens, or eavesdrop. Many of the conversations are happening simultaneously, so their decisions determine what they learn and who they impress.

1:45 P.M.

The Middenheim party arrives along with the Characters. The Emperor’s party is already in the pavilion with ‘Karl-Franz’ on a throne-like chair in the centre, overlooking the artillery ground. There are formal greetings between Graf Boris and ‘Karl-Franz’ before anyone takes a seat.

@UUID[Actor.6eNwY93t5wjxPYOs]{Colonel Sievers} salutes the Emperor and attempts to approach, but one of the High Helms politely tells him later would be preferable. An observer can take an Opposed Test — Intuition vs von Fielbach’s Cool to notice ‘Karl-Franz’ did not recognise the colonel. @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Thugenheim} explains Sievers’ identity to @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina}, adding that he has an impressive reputation but it’s unusual to see him in the city rather than campaigning in the mountains.

2:00 P.M.

Just as the parade begins, @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} sweeps in and gives ‘Karl-Franz’ and Boris an elegant wave. She speaks loudly for all to hear, ‘What a gathering. It rather reminds me of the event your father arranged for your 16th birthday, Your Majesty.’ The ‘Emperor’ smiles and nods.

The parade begins accompanied by a cadence of clapping from the crowd. @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Thugenheim} is enthusiastic. Most of the group watch attentively, but @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug}, @UUID[Actor.1Fw8roY9zezj0jAn]{Immanuel-Ferrand}, and @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} talk amongst themselves. @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina} offers to introduce the Characters to anyone other than the Emperor, Yorri, or Volkmar.

2:15 P.M.

A servant passes around the room with goblets of wine. @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle} and @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug} are deep in conversation, but as they sip the wine, the high ambassador splutters: ‘What is this? Reik water?’ The countess laughs, tastes hers, and pulls a face: ‘Ugh. Someone should have a word with Ermine.’ She points at a sour-faced woman — @UUID[Actor.x2cF45W4cU4QQW8v]{Ermine Liebwitz von Decker und Hanulf}, a distant relation of Emmanuelle and steward of the Imperial Wine Cellars. The Characters could take this cue and persuade Ermine to bring a better vintage with an Average (+20) Bribery Test or a threat to her position. They shall meet her again in @UUID[JournalEntry.mAUuZ2hUO5TrG30w]{Chapter 7}.

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} asks @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar} and @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric} to enlighten him on how their cults fare against worshippers of the Ruinous Powers. The two priests give pious and pointed responses intended to make the other look lax. If they are close, Zuntermein addresses the Characters, ‘I believe you have exposed some followers of the Ruinous Powers in Middenheim — am I correct?’ Their response affects their standing with the Sigmarite or Ulrican factions, depending on whether Middenheim comes out of their account badly.
