Having completed his long pilgrimage in the footsteps of Kemmler, he heard some evidence that the University of Streissan might hold copies of some particularly ancient books on the intertwining of Necromancy and Chaos. Though this was far from certain to be the case, the Characters’ presence at the first siege of Streissan has, in @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber’s} mind, cemented the rumour as absolute fact. After all, the Characters are his greatest nemeses, and so must have gone there to vex him. The fact that he comes across them again, having returned to the town, only makes him more certain they are there to hide from him the very knowledge he seeks.

The town, ravaged by war, is the perfect backdrop for his final victory over the Characters and the resurrection of the great Heinrich Kemmler, who at least in @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber’s} mind, will recognise the Gravelord as an equal at last

The Alarm

Events kick off as the Characters, having found Master Albertus Nyman, are departing the town. If they have avoided Leitdorf ’s interest, it is merely unnerving. If they are actively fleeing his forces, they might already feel on edge. As they approach the gates, a bell peals out over the town. The deserted streets remain so for a moment, but as the bell rings on, troops begin to rush to the walls, and private homes open doors and windows so that those within can assess the situation. The sound is one of the three warning bells of Streissan, a mighty dull iron monument that hangs above the town’s temple of Morr — it is only rung when there is threat of Undead assaulting the town. Most have never heard its tone outside of a yearly ceremony, and it is enough of a novelty that even the worried citizens of Streissan take an interest.

Upon reaching the walls, it is clear that escape has become (more) difficult. A host of soldiers is gathering around the town, still a ways off but numbering in the thousands. They are heading to lines occupied by Alptraum’s soldiers some days or weeks prior, and threaten to surround the town in short order. The host carries tall banners, black and bearing, of course, a great skull. Those with a telescope can see that they are mostly Skeletons and Zombies, though @UUID[Actor.FRS2PzhU3H98XfTX]{Flying Death Skulls}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.actors.KE2xU8UltLaCnulO]{Carrion}, and other fell things fly above the oncoming army.

If the Characters are attempting to leave by the city gates, they are turned back, fanciful talk of their having Ghal Maraz forgotten for the moment. Any attempt to sneak out results in the Characters fumbling into the hands, or claws, of @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber’s} forces. You should give the Characters an opportunity to retreat back to the town, where ladders may be thrown down for them — either to assist in their rescue, or to seize the Hammer if the troops are aware of it.

The army is an Undead force commanded by @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber}. Currently led by Krell, its orders are to approach openly and draw attention away from what Gräber plans to do next: sneak into the university.

An Interesting Approach

Any Character who makes a successful Challenging (+0) Lore (Undead) Test notices the following:

1 SL: A couple of Carrion are hovering over the vanguard, keeping pace with it rather than ranging ahead. If the Character has encountered @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} before, they may be expecting to see him riding a @UUID[Actor.UgNmlQAzZKlmRy5j]{Flying Nightmare}, but it is nowhere in sight.

2+ SL: There do not seem to be any ethereal Undead anywhere in the force.

While it is obvious to anyone that the army is making no attempt to approach stealthily, any Character who makes a successful Challenging (+0) Lore (Warfare) Test notices that it seems to be doing everything it can to announce its arrival. Drums are booming, banners are flying, and the ranks seem spread out a little wider than usual to make the force seem larger than it is.

What the Characters make of this information is up to the Players. The fact is that @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} wants all eyes on the approaching army so that he and his ethereal detachment can enter the town unnoticed, taking the inhabitants by surprise.

Preparations

The Characters have a few minutes to observe Streissan’s preparations to meet the attack. In response to the alarm bell, those forces still in good order collect weapons and take up positions on the wall. Non-combatants — the old, the sick, and the less able — have all long been confined to their homes, but nevertheless a few boisterous elderly folk attempt to join the defence. Word has quickly spread that the enemy are Undead and despite days of persecution at the hands of @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Marius Leitdorf ’s} forces, the threat of being eaten alive by a shambling horde of monstrosities does much towards unifying the town’s citizens. Priests of Morr and Sigmar, who had avoided taking a political stance on the siege and takeover of Streissan, emerge to bolster morale. Many begin to pray, calling on Sigmar to grant Miracles and Blessings that strengthen the town’s walls and gates against the approaching Undead. Pigeons are released, bound for Averheim, Nuln, and Altdorf with news of the attack. With weapons ready and eyes fixed on the foe, the defenders of Streissan wait.

The Hammer and The Priest

If Leitdorf is aware of the Hammer and his forces become aware of the Characters’ presence during preparations, Leitdorf offers them a final opportunity to give him the weapon willingly or be killed. Father Olaf, an elderly priest of Sigmar, inserts himself into this standoff asking to see the Hammer. If the Characters show it to him, the old Sigmarite instantly falls to the ground before it. After a powerful moment he arises, the fire of a younger man alight in his eyes. Father Olaf chastises @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf}, telling him:

‘Those that bear the Hammer of Sigmar are his Chosen Few, and to block their passage is to spit upon the Heldenhammer himself.’

The old priest’s voice carries unnaturally far and with a shuddering presence, enough to cow any immediate threat of violence from anyone save @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf} himself. Drawing his blade, he looks set to act, before his horse, Daisy, strides towards Father Olaf and begins to eat his hat. The awe and tension of the moment evaporates as Leitdorf laughs aloud and sheaths his blade.

He fully intends to seize the Characters and take Ghal Maraz before they leave the town, but for now he lets them be.

The Old School Spirits

Just as the Characters start to think about what they should be doing, a terrible sound comes from the university, carrying over the din of preparations. A terrible scream, inhuman and chilling to the very bone, echoes over Streissan. In the silence that follows, far more Human screams are heard faintly coming from the university — the Gravelord has arrived.

If the Characters head to the university, they see a group of ethereal Undead creatures passing through the walls of the buildings that make up the campus. There is one @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.hMbcLVjk7eUdxtqC]{Cairn Wraith} for each Character (you can alter the numbers as needed if the party is particularly strong or weak), plus one @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.TWy5l4uYTRAtjfit]{Tomb Banshee} and @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} himself, who has cast @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.Item.pxgEQNMfuq1R9Thr]{Spirit Walk} to make himself @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal}.

If the Characters do not go to the university, it quickly becomes clear that they should. The Undead outside the city launch feints and minor attacks, holding back the great bulk of their forces, while survivors of the university attack swarm the walls, attempting to get out of the city rather than remain with the ghosts inside. If the Characters still refuse to head to the university, worry not — @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} will come for them soon enough.

Gräber’s Plan

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is using his army’s approach as a diversion to cover the incursion of his ethereal force. Once in the university, he plans to slaughter the defenders and send his @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.TWy5l4uYTRAtjfit]{Tomb Banshee} and @UUID[Actor.6w0OKlsdgKqfW78D]{Hexwraiths} to surprise the city’s defenders from within, just as the army outside is attacking. Meanwhile, Gräber himself plans to ransack the library for the forbidden books he is sure are kept there. While he will discover some chronicles that tell of Sigmar’s battle against Krell and the career of Heinrich Kemmler, he does not find the lores of necromantic knowledge he seeks. Gräber soon realises that they are no longer present — a chancellor of the university long ago burned the foul things, which Nyman can confirm if the Characters learn of Gräber’s plans and think to ask him. Gräber, for his part, assumes the Characters took them when they were in the city earlier and swiftly turns his attention, and his wrath, on them.

Contact with the Enemy

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is not expecting the Characters to be at the university — he had not realised they returned to the town after their earlier visit. Their presence will complicate his position considerably and convince him even further that they are an elite force of witch hunters sent by the Emperor himself to hunt him down. Gräber’s reaction is a mixture of frustration at the obstacle the party represents and satisfaction that his arch-nemeses have appeared once more, confirming his own opinion of his importance.

Our Weapons Are Useless!

Creatures with the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal} Trait can be trouble, as some parties simply have no way to deal with them. Only magical attacks can damage them, and while the Characters have had some opportunities throughout The Enemy Within to acquire such weapons, they are only really guaranteed to possess Ghal Maraz at this point. Leaving a single Character to deal with all of these creatures may be a tall order. Miracles and magic also work against Ethereal creatures, but if the party does not have any other way to deal with the creatures, you may wish to change up the encounter. A priest of Sigmar or Morr may be on hand to work a Miracle or Blessing, such as @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.2WN0muIB2BFd4kBO]{Blessing of Righteousness}, that will allow a Character to harm the spirits, or they may be fewer in number. Priests of Morr can also create special oils that allow a weapon to harm spirits, though these are rare and expensive to create, so any priest will only have a little to hand. Alternatively, the ward which protects the restricted section may temporarily make all the spirits present sufficiently manifest for them to be harmed by mundane weapons. Such an effect would be brief, perhaps 2–3 rounds, but would give the Characters some time to strike back against the dead.).

Ghostsmear

Though Priests of Morr refer to it reverentially as Morr’s Blessed Oil, most who have had cause to use the shimmering tincture in battling the undead refer to it as ‘Ghostsmear’ or simply ‘The Good Stuff.’ Spirits, spectres, ghosts, banshees and other ethereal undead that would normally only be harmed by magical weapons can be damaged by a weapon coated in Ghostsmear. One application lasts an hour under ideal conditions, but may be washed from the blade sooner if it is raining heavily or the blade becomes submerged. Additionally, if the weapon is used to injure a living creature while covered in Ghostsmear, the effect is instantly dismissed as the infusion of living blood renders the oil inert.

Ghostsmear is never offered for sale, but only created at need by devout priests of Morr. It requires 3 Gold Crowns worth of ingredients and a night of fevered prayer to create. Ghostsmear can be stored for one year before losing its effects.’

However, the Characters are likely quite powerful by now, and have had plenty of warning that @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is a threat to them. If they failed to prepare properly, you may simply wish to let the spirits do some serious harm to them. This is WFRP, after all, and Fate points exist for a reason!

To @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber}, there could be no greater affirmation of his destiny soon reaching its zenith than the presence of his greatest enemies here, at the mercy of the greatest army he has ever commanded.

Before entering combat, @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} casts a number of protective spells on himself, in addition to the one that makes him @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal}. These are @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.pHITBuvCatCOBhZb]{Aethyric Armour} (which he can extend as described in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.YBVrpUHEjohB1H4f.JournalEntryPage.SCijiCw628GLE2pT#arcane-spells]{Arcane Spells}), @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNMQQhBYzHoRq7AD]{Distracting}, and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.J0wUSVSnos7fBprP]{Terrifying}. All four of these spells have a Duration of Willpower Bonus Rounds, and will expire four rounds after combat is joined.

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} spends the first round making one of his bombastic speeches, and as usual its dramatic impact is somewhat lessened by his small stature and whining, nasal voice. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.TWy5l4uYTRAtjfit]{The Tomb Banshee} hovers by his side as he speaks, and the @UUID[Actor.6w0OKlsdgKqfW78D]{Hexwraiths} form a screen in front of him, ready to fight anyone who tries to approach.

‘So, we meet again! The Gravelord commends your persistence, but this time there will be no mercy! Prepare to die, and serve the Gravelord forever! Attack, my children!’

At his command, the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.TWy5l4uYTRAtjfit]{Tomb Banshee} begins a @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.TWy5l4uYTRAtjfit.Item.sy2x2WifRcIWohoM]{Ghostly Howl} and one @UUID[Actor.6w0OKlsdgKqfW78D]{Hexwraith} moves to fight each Character. Any ‘spare’ Hexwraiths begin slaughtering anyone else about or gang up on the most dangerous Character, especially any @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} knows to be capable of spellcasting or commanding Miracles.

If confronted at the university, @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} makes his way to the library, an imposing old building of stone with a much less imposing thatched roof. To continue his search (passing through the shelves in his @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal} state), he heads for the Restricted Collection. Any Characters who try to follow him have to negotiate the walls, locked doors, and a maze of shelves, which means that he will probably reach the door to the Restricted Collection first. Though he will not find what he is searching for there, the section does contain many dangerous books, and a previous chancellor hired a wizard to set several wards upon it. The wards dispel Gräber’s @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.Item.pxgEQNMfuq1R9Thr]{Spirit Walk}, and he will have to deal with the inconvenience of corporeality.

If the Characters are elsewhere, such as hiding out in the Nyman basement or helping defend the walls, then @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} eventually finds them and attacks them directly. He pauses first to compliment their cunning in retrieving the books he seeks before he could get there, which doubtless leaves them confused..

The Attack Begins

Regardless of whether or not the Characters are at the university, once @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} reaches the Restricted Section his @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.Item.pxgEQNMfuq1R9Thr]{Spirit Walk} spell comes to an end and he becomes fully material. At the same time, screams and crashes ring out from the town walls as the main Undead force attacks. If the Characters are at the walls, they may sensibly wish to help defend them. While the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.Mt5JAoOSaEH1PdcP]{Skeletons} and @UUID[Actor.ukxsdiMsSlzLHMm3]{Zombies} have some trouble scaling the walls, their numbers quickly add up. The Undead throw up crude ladders of lashed-together bone, and the nimbler Skeletons attempt to assault anyone defending the walls. @UUID[Actor.FRS2PzhU3H98XfTX]{Flying Death Skulls} assault defenders from the air, along with other flying Undead.

The Shelves

During any fight in the library, there is a very good chance that a Player will think of tipping the bookcases over to stop @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} reaching the restricted section, to crush or escape from some Undead attacker, or for some other reason.

The bookcases in the university’s library are huge and heavy in proportion. Double-faced and made of oak planks an inch thick, they stand 8 feet high, 12 feet long, and 2 feet deep. Each one holds books totalling several hundred pounds in weight. This weight makes them hard to tip, at least initially.

To get a shelf unit to a tipping point requires a Very Hard (-30) Strength Test. Up to eight Characters and NPCs can co-operate in pushing one shelf over (see @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.NS3YGlJQxwTggjRX.JournalEntryPage.lQThXbnpgQ30VBXR#assistance]{Assistance}). As the bookcase tips, books will begin to slide from the shelves on the side opposite the Characters pushing it. They will rain down on anyone beneath, causing a Damage [[/r 3d10 # Damage]] hit on any creature in the way who fails a Difficult (-10) Dodge Test — though of course @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal} creatures are immune. A Critical Success on the Strength Test leads to a domino effect. Instead of ending up leaning against its neighbour, the falling bookcase knocks that one over too, and so on until a bookcase either hits a wall or falls into an empty space.!

@UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf ’s} troops were unprepared — some are drunk, others injured from the battle. The defence is desperate. There should be some kind of Undead for each Character to attack every round, though in the cut and thrust of mass combat, it is difficult to make any real progress. The presence of Ghal Maraz, if it is drawn, bolsters the defenders, and any section of wall where the bearer of the great hammer stands is defended bitterly and with success.

After he is finished in the university, or when things start to go badly for him if the Characters are there, @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} tries to cast a @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.jdv7gnwKk6eEPtQK]{Marsh Lights} spell and send the lights out through the main window. This is a pre-arranged signal to his Undead force, and a barrage of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.HqInHmOviuLqymdm]{Screaming Skulls} strikes the window on the next round, shattering the glass and offering Gräber a potential escape route.

Combat

By this stage, battle has been joined between the defenders of Streissan and the attacking Undead. You can resolve this battle in a number of different ways; three possibilities are offered below:

The Mass Combat Rules: Archives of the Empire II contains rules for mass combat. They can be used to cover the party’s experience of the battle, though you should do this only if the Characters enjoy larger combats. Elsewhere in Empire in Ruins the Characters find themselves at another siege if they attempt to renew Ghal Maraz, and again at Diesdorf if you use the additional material @UUID[JournalEntry.ZeJj1Sg9PGwUgCbj]{The Siege of Diesdorf} in this book, all of which could use the mass combat rules. Be aware that the Characters may well become fatigued from finding themselves in the midst of such battles, though others might find it a suitably epic experience as the campaign nears its end. You should play this by ear, and attempt to cater to your Players’ preferences.

Defend the Walls!: The walls of Streissan are assaulted from all directions, and some areas risk being quickly overrun if the Characters don’t pitch in. Defenders sound horns from distressed areas; if the Characters aren’t aware of what this means a nearby soldier quickly fills them in — someone is almost overrun. If the Characters respond to this call, they find [[/br 1d10 # Soldiers]] beleaguered soldiers holding out against a group of Undead that have scaled or breached the walls.

You can use the table provided, or select the numbers yourself. If any Character makes a successful Challenging (+0) Leadership Test, the soldiers obey their orders and any survivors continue to follow them once the combat is resolved. This Test becomes Average (+20) if the Character wields Ghal Maraz. The Characters might be able to gather a force around them to retake the walls.

Flee!: The Characters may well attempt to flee the town, leaving it to its fate. If they have found Nyman, the Characters have all the information they require. If not, they will have to live without being able to renew @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.eE8H6wRoq0GGpWR8]{Ghal Maraz} — see @UUID[JournalEntry.pHsN1cclx1uQlvSH.JournalEntryPage.Xtd2fjpAJtenwMIo#the-skull-splitter-has-returned]{The Skull Splitter Has Returned}.

The docks are a likely path to freedom. Though they are under siege by Undead emerging from the river, @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is no tactician and underestimated the flow of the river. Many of his forces are carried away downstream, likely to confuse and terrify some fisherfolk near Nuln in the near future. The Characters may grab a boat or raft here with relative ease, seeing off the few waterlogged Undead who cling to it, and flee. This is not the most heroic response, but it is certainly the safest. @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf} will eventually hold Streissan, but at a terrible loss, and his convincing victory and claim to the seat of Elector is again thrown into doubt. More civil strife will result, and the Gravelord will survive to trouble the Empire further. Despite his theatrical bluster, Gräber clearly has a gift for Necromancy, and though the Characters may have laughed at him in the past, they are unlikely to be quite so full of mirth should they cross his path again.

Ending the Attack

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber’s} Undead force breaks off its attack on the monastery as soon as one of the following conditions is fulfilled:

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is killed; see @UUID[.eEED4CxEAA0TqLQR#the-gravelord-falls]{The Gravelord Falls} below.

The Character bearing @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.eE8H6wRoq0GGpWR8]{Ghal Maraz} rolls an Astounding Success (6+ SL) on a Challenging (+0) Leadership Test to command the troops defending the town; see @UUID[.eEED4CxEAA0TqLQR#heroes-of-the-day]{Heroes of the Day} below.

The Characters appear to be utterly doomed and need rescue; see @UUID[.eEED4CxEAA0TqLQR#the-wrath-of-sigmar]{The Wrath of Sigmar} below.

As the GM, you can also end the attack if anything else happens that makes it appropriate in dramatic terms for the Undead to retreat. The following paragraphs may provide some inspiration for how to bring this about.

@Table[random-undead]

The Gravelord’s Army

A definitive list of @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber’s} Undead army is not given here. This is deliberate.

As GM, you must decide in advance how you are going to run this incident. Depending on the choice you make, a hard-and-fast army list may be unnecessary. It can also be damaging to the campaign experience.

While the party is certainly stronger by now than they were at the start of the campaign, their actual combat strength could vary widely, according to the Careers and Skills they have taken, the equipment they have bought or otherwise acquired, and various other factors. Any attempt to provide a ‘one size fits all’ army list would be doomed to failure: either in the form of a demoralising ‘total party kill’ or as an enemy scarcely worthy of the name. Only you know your Players and their Characters, and only you can decide what would make a suitably challenging foe.

Therefore, we recommend that before running this part of the adventure, take a little time to plan. Look over the available range of Undead creatures, both in the WFRP rulebook and in other sources (such as the previous Gravelord adventures). Choose the creatures that make the most sense, add any that you think would make things more interesting for the Characters, and be prepared to adjust numbers on the fly if things turn out to be too easy or too hard.

A Strategic Retreat

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber}, as ever, underestimates his opposition. He certainly did not expect the Characters to be carrying the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.eE8H6wRoq0GGpWR8]{Ghal Maraz}. Once he realises the books he sought are not here, and once he has convinced himself that the Characters do not have them, he retreats. Whatever troops he has available continue to attack the Characters, attempting to distract them, and the troops attacking the walls continue their assault, though their strength is diminished once the Gravelord has fled.

The Characters can try to pursue @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} — they are very likely to want to put a final end to him. He flees into the nearest open area, and after two rounds, his @UUID[Actor.UgNmlQAzZKlmRy5j]{Winged Nightmare} swoops down and picks him up, its talons barely grazing the battlements and rooftops as it struggles into the air. Under cover of a barrage of missile fire from the Undead army, he abandons the attack, leaving masses of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.actors.Mt5JAoOSaEH1PdcP]{Skeletons} and @UUID[Actor.ukxsdiMsSlzLHMm3]{Zombies} to fight a rearguard as the army withdraws.

If @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is killed in the course of his escape attempt, refer to The Gravelord Falls below.

The Gravelord Falls

@UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} has been a thorn in the party’s side for some time now, and few things would be more satisfying to the Players than to bring him down — especially here, at the zenith of his power, where none can possibly deny the threat he poses. It smacks of poetic justice, and the Characters’ role in his defeat goes a long way to ensuring their safe exit from the town, as @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Marius Leitdorf} should almost certainly be aware of the presence of Ghal Maraz by the battle’s end, if he wasn’t before. He seeks to claim it, but if the Characters slew the dread necromancer who assaulted Streissan in full view of his soldiers, @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf} has no option other than to let them go.

The Characters may have killed @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber}, or come close to doing so, in one of the previous encounters. Their best chance was in the village of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.journals.aNYMrBowuSB7g7wd.JournalEntryPage.C05XMKlAGcic9fXj]{Pritzstock} during the events of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.actors.FRS2PzhU3H98XfTX]{Flying Death Skulls}. If so, the Players might be enormously frustrated by his return and eager to put a permanent end to this dangerous — and profoundly irritating — foe. If @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} falls at Streissan, you have a choice:

Victory!: The Characters have prevailed. @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is dead — truly dead this time — and bereft of their master, his Undead followers crumble to dust and blow away on the breeze. This is particularly appropriate if the killing blow was struck by Ghal Maraz, as it is an ancient enemy to Necromancers, having long ago been used by Sigmar to overcome the Necromancer Morath at Brass Keep. Priests of Morr gather up the Gravelord’s mortal remains and subject them to a series of divine rituals that ensure that Gräber is utterly destroyed, in body and soul, forever. The Characters can escape the town and are free to carry on with Empire in Ruins.

A Cunning Plan: @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} has also been frustrated by his various encounters with the Characters, and his natural overconfidence has been tempered somewhat. While scouring the vaults for traces of Krell and Kemmler, he recovered a rare Nehekaran scarab amulet, which he wears out of sight inside his clothing. Upon his death, the scarab frees his spirit as a ghost, crumbling to dust as it does so, and he either escapes or the Characters might manage to chase the Ghost down and destroy it. If he escapes, Gräber is @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.tNWrJUOArwfWXsPw]{Ethereal} in the next encounter. If the Ghost is destroyed, refer to Victory! above.

Heroes of the Day

While the Characters may well be enemies of @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Marius Leitdorf} and pursued by his troops, all that is put aside during the Undead attack. The troops are weakened by their occupation of the town, and the possibility of an Undead horde was far from anyone’s mind. They are prepared to defend the walls, as a counterattack by the Alptraums was always a possibility, but had thought any counter-attack would take weeks to muster. The Characters are likely skilled combatants and certainly have experience fighting the Gravelord and his undead. They also bear Ghal Maraz, which will likely become obvious during the battle.

If the Characters find themselves fighting on the walls, and a Character scores an Astounding Success on a Challenging (+0) Leadership Test, the troops begin to rally to them. Much of @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf ’s} leadership takes a long time to get organised, and the sight of an inspiring Character, shouting words of encouragement and striking down Undead left and right is an inspiring one. The nearby forces swiftly rally to the Character, pushing the Undead back all around them. If the Father Olaf made an appearance earlier to mediate for the Characters with Leitdorf, he appears again now, invoking Sigmar and calling all to resist the Undead. Leitdorf ’s forces temporarily gain the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.aE3pyW20Orvdjzj0]{Hatred (Undead)} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.RyxOZqcBNZ7Zw721]{Holy Hatred} Talents at maximum level until the battle is over, but it will likely be more than enough to describe the narrative as the rallied troops overwhelm the Undead attackers. The creatures are cast back from the walls and pursued mercilessly into the plains beyond.

A brief time later, the surviving Undead pull back (if @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} is alive) or turn to dust, should he fall in the battle (See @UUID[.eEED4CxEAA0TqLQR#the-gravelord-falls]{The Gravelord Falls}, above).

The Wrath of Sigmar

If, and only if, the Characters are completely overwhelmed and likely to perish, you may consider having Father Olaf return for a final strike against the Gravelord. Wielding an old carpenter’s hammer, glowing brightly with holy might, he emerges from the melee to strike at @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber}. The blow lands true, but the Gravelord is only staggered. Gräber turns and with a blast of necromantic energy casts @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.O7G5olv0aWLpb7Ea]{Drain}, withering the old priest to a dried husk in moments. Still, he is staggered, and the hammer’s blow had a touch of the divine about it. Unwilling to risk himself further, the Gravelord flees the battlefield (see @UUID[.eEED4CxEAA0TqLQR#a-strategic-retreat]{A Strategic Retreat}, above).

This should be an embarrassment for the Characters, as @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} once again escapes their grasp. Not being the heroes of the hour, they still have to deal with escaping Leitdorf ’s grasp.

The Aftermath

The Undead are in full retreat, and if @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} has fallen many of them will have crumbled to dust. The soldiers begin the task of cleaning up, while priests of Morr prepare the dead for burial with more care than usual, should the Undead influence have spread to their bodies. What remains of the Undead is burned in a great pyre that lasts for days, and chokes the sky above Striessan even further.

Part Four: What Now?.name: Part Four: What Now?
Part Four: What Now?.text:
After this battle, if he still lives, the Characters may decide that @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} needs to be stopped once and for all, distracting them from the main plot of Empire in Ruins. @UUID[.8L3uksY6Wp6nq65G#pursuit]{The Pursuit} section gives some options for making sure that Gräber is able to give the Characters the slip so they can carry on with the adventure. The section in @UUID[.ekkuWCV5NiMootnT#handling-the-rumours]{Part Two, Handling the Rumours}, offers some more ideas, including the option of letting the Characters follow Gräber.

Alternatively, you may decide that the Characters have had enough of @UUID[Actor.r4AUsjsfOL9HW8lO]{Gräber} by now — he certainly is annoying — and simply let him die and stay dead. This is an especially good choice if the Characters were particularly heroic in defeating him — there is still much adventure to come, and the Characters may well be humbled yet on their return to Altdorf. Let them have the moment, granting them @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Leitdorf} ’s mercurial respect for just long enough to see them safely from Streissan and back upon the path of Empire in Ruins.

Experience Points Awards

You can award the following Experience Points for this adventure, with bonus awards for bright ideas and good roleplaying.

@Exp[25,Defended the walls.]{25 points for defending the walls.}

@Exp[50,Stopped Gräber at the university]{50 points if they stop Gräber at the university}

@Exp[50,Rallied the defenders and drive back the Undead]{50 points if they rally the defenders and drive back the Undead}

@Exp[100,Finally killed Gräber]{100 points each for finally killing Gräber}

Chilly Reception.name: Chilly Reception
Chilly Reception.text:
In this chapter, the Characters reach Middenheim and witness growing anger towards Sigmarites and the south. They act as observers of a last-ditch attempt to calm the religious division between the Ulricans and the Sigmarites. @UUID[Actor.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Yorri XV}, the Grand Theogonist of Sigmar, sends one of his greatest minds to Middenheim: High Capitular @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar von Hindenstern}.

Volkmar has proposals to deliver. He wants @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric} to journey to the @UUID[Scene.Jt9P7OoOEQIrG1TK]{Shrine of the Shining Rock} in order to make a grand gesture of unity and, to sweeten the deal, a request on behalf of @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince Wolfgang}, the Emperor’s nephew and heir apparent, to wed @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina Todbringer}.

Crowd Control.name: Crowd Control
Crowd Control.text:
The roads get busier as the Characters draw close to Middenheim. In this time of uncertainty, people are flocking to the city, fleeing from raiders or hoping to sign up with Middenheim’s forces for the war that now seems ineluctable. There are long lines of distressed and agitated people at the entrances to the city.

In an attempt to control the influx and maintain a semblance of order, booths have been set up before each entrance as city officials question everyone who wants to enter. Commercial cargoes are waved through, as is anyone who can prove they live in Middenheim, but refugees are directed to clusters of tents that stand on either side of the road, where impatient crowds are building up. The Characters have no trouble getting into the city. If @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} is with them, a squad of watchmen rushes them to the nearest gate, pushing aside anyone in the way. If they are on their own, the Ducal commissions that Graf Boris gave them for their mission to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.journals.z5Rjl2Tmbabj1i3b]{Picket} in The Horned Rat is sufficient to have them waved through.

@UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Heinrich} spends a minute in conversation with the guard. If Characters listen in and pass a Difficult (–10) Perception Test they hear muttered phrases. ‘Arrived without warning’, ‘something of an imposition’, and ‘reckon they must be getting desperate down there if they’ll resort to this sort of thing’. It is the guard who speaks, Heinrich keeps his voice low.

If Characters ask @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Heinrich} what was said he says, ‘looks like we will be finding out soon enough’; if they press him further he says, ‘a delegation has arrived from Altdorf, led by High Capitular @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar}, an adjunct to Sigmar’s Grand Theogonist’.

Inside the City

Inside the city the streets are as packed as they were at the start of Middenheim’s Carnival in Power Behind the Throne, but the mood is very different — frantic rather than elated.

Refugees scuttle through the streets, carrying their possessions on their backs, or pushing them in carts as they scour the city for a place to stay. Every flophouse and hostelry is full to overflowing. Stables, warehouses, and derelict buildings are crammed with people. In places thugs are busy turfing out unfortunates who can no longer pay for a patch of damp stone floor.

Most of Middenheim’s Sigmarites have fled the city or keep themselves indoors, but accusations of Sigmarite tendencies or southern sympathies are being used to settle old scores and target folk who never quite fitted in. In the Freiburg, the temple of Sigmar is surrounded by a dozen bored-looking watchmen. They take jeers from passers-by with good humour, but do nothing to prevent the walls being daubed with anti-Sigmarite slogans — though they step in to prevent serious damage. The Characters’ can reach the palace safely without incident or attracting unwanted attention, but if they decide to become involved in a situation play it out.

Rumours.name: Rumours
Rumours.text:
Rumours

Along the way, the Characters have a chance to pick up the latest news and rumours. As always, they are a mixture of truth, half-truth, and outright fiction.

  • Graf Boris has declared himself the ‘Wolf Emperor,’ reviving a centuries old title. It’s a sure sign that the north is breaking away — and not before time! Those pampered fools in Altdorf have had their way for too long!’

    The Graf has made no such announcement, though there are plenty in Middenheim who would like him to do so.

  • The Greenskins are getting restless down south, and there has been fighting in Black Fire Pass. If the Empire is weakened by civil war they could overrun the south — unless the stalwart Counts of Sylvania and Averheim stop squabbling and put a stop to them.

    This refers to an @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.mbXVJGCGSm8m7ANd.JournalEntryPage.LwuezrkCidrmlovt]{earlier rumour} that interpreted the return of the Imperial Ostlanders as a sign that the Greenskins had been defeated. In fact, the opposite is true, and Colonel Sievers is in Altdorf to persuade the Emperor to strengthen the southern border.

  • There’s going to be trouble in Ubersreik. The Jungfreuds are recruiting troops and planning to take the town back by force, and damn the Emperor. If the north secedes, the Emperor’s word will lose all its power and the south will probably fall apart.

    Half-true. The Jungfreuds are angry at being ousted from Ubersreik, but their recruiting is mainly aimed at protecting themselves from their long-standing enemies.

  • There have been more battles on the border between Ostland and Talabecland, in defiance of the Emperor’s orders to stand down. The Tassenincks still blame Grand Duke Gustav von Krieglitz of Talabecland for the death of Crown Prince Hergard in the Grey Mountains, and with Middenheim looking ready to establish a breakaway Wolf Empire in the north, Talabecland could very well do the same, splitting the Empire in three.

    True, but incomplete. While it is true that Talabeclanders have never been fond of Reiklanders and Altdorf’s rule is resented by many, there is no organised movement to secede.

  • The Sigmarites are starting to give way over the religious troubles. Some of them still want to burn every good Ulrican, but the Grand Theogonist has sent one of his scholars to Middenheim for talks to resolve the whole business of heresy.

    True. Grand Theogonist Yorri XV has sent High Capitular Volkmar to conduct talks with Ar-Ulric.

  • The Emperor hasn’t been seen in public for a while, according to some traders from Altdorf. They say he’s busy trying to hold the Empire together, but more likely he’s laying low for fear of Ulrican assassins.

    Partially true. Emperor Karl-Franz has been in seclusion as the Characters find out later in this adventure.

  • The cult of Ulric has chosen Emil Valgeir as our new Ar-Ulric. This is one in the eye for the Sigmarites, Emil’s no milksop. He won’t brook disrespect of our traditions.

    True.

  • The Emperor is dead, and has been replaced by a double that the court keeps around for security purposes. Someone at the court is ruling from the shadows in the dead Emperor’s name!

    Partially true, the Emperor is very ill but his double is making public appearances to cover up the fact.

  • Southern rulers are using the Mutant Edict as a cover, recruiting Mutants and other creatures of Chaos into their armies as they prepare to march on Altdorf. This wicked law must be struck down, and Mutants consigned to the cleansing flames as they have always been.

    Untrue, though most Witch Hunters and many other Sigmarites are fully prepared to believe it.

  • Relations between Middenland and Stirland are uneasy. Stirland is a centre of Sigmarite belief, and has made strong representations to Middenland over the persecution of Sigmarite priests there. Grand Duke Leopold von Bildhofen of Middenland treats these complaints with barely disguised contempt. His public pronouncements are that he knows nothing of any attacks on Sigmarites.

    True.

  • The harvest has not been good this year. Grain has not grown well, although fruit is sound. Merchants are rubbing their hands at the thought of higher prices and fatter profits. There have already been bread riots in some cities.

    True.

    The Crown Prince is a mutant, you know — with a tail and wings! That’s why he hasn’t been seen outside Castle Reikguard for ages, and it’s why the Emperor has banned the killing of mutants.

    False, but the Characters may well have heard this rumour or one like it before now.

  • Minor nobles across the north are planning to denounce all followers of Sigmar as heretics! It can only be a matter of time before Graf Boris Todbringer gives his support to a religious war, and any Sigmarites who haven’t fled before then will surely be burned!

    Things have not gone quite this far, but plenty of Sigmarites believe this rumour.

  • I saw a cat with two heads, eight legs and two tails. It heralds disaster I tell you! Disaster! Pardon! Two cats? I know what I saw.

Bearers of Blood Demonstration.name: Bearers of Blood Demonstration
Bearers of Blood Demonstration.text:
As the Characters make their way towards the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.SbaXkT2ZupAWRthT]{Middenpalaz}, they pass through the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.Non5YhyYgrHDW6mB]{Square of Martials}. There is a loud public demonstration occurring to one side of the square. There are a number of men and women standing around a hastily erected wooden platform. Their Ulrican sympathies are obvious at a glance. They are dressed in furs, many wearing wolf pelts with jaws and claws still attached, and they carry talismans such as the wolf ’s head and the axe.

@UUID[Actor.pdf8ECaWC0ZAapKB]{Beate Moser}, a tall, striking young woman with broad shoulders and long white hair is the most vocal of the group She stands on the platform and delivers an excoriating polemic against Sigmarites, Altdorfers, and Ulrican moderates. Her tirade is peppered with allusions to Ulrican lore, a sample runs along these lines.

‘The City of the White Wolf stomached the unseemly presence of one High Capitular of Sigmar, but we do not abide the presence of a second! Hindenstern must be sent back to Altdorf with his tail between his legs! Middenheim’s misguided citizens who venerate Sigmar, Hammer of the Elderly, are merely tolerated — not welcomed! We knew mewling Jarrick was unfit to bear the Hammer Axe of Skoll, as are all those who do not feel Ulric’s own blood rush through their veins! Now his brother has been granted his office. He may not have Ulric’s blood, but he could at least bear his teeth and rid us of this turbulent Capitular!’

@UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} and @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim} make for the palace gates. Characters who try to read their reactions notice on a Hard (–20) Intuition Test that they seem confused.

If either of them is asked about the demonstration, they say, ‘These people are extremists. The Sons of Ulric preach that only a person who can trace their ancestry to Ulric ought to be anointed as his High Priest. Of course, the official cult does not agree. Last thing I knew, they were banned from holding assembly in the city, obviously something has changed.’

This is true. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.OCwl83kq8339cIHj.JournalEntryPage.v89vatY0D7lynlCA]{The Sons of Ulric} may not respect the new Ar-Ulric, @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Emil Valgeir}, but he has grudging admiration for them, and has lifted the prohibition on them gathering and demonstrating in Middenheim.

A Character wondering about the providence of the phrase ‘Hammer of the Elderly’ could work it out by passing a Hard (–20) Lore (Theology) Test. During his campaign to unify the Empire, Sigmar slew King Artur, then an old man, in order to bring Middenheim within his rule. It isn’t considered a polite thing to highlight, but it is one of the grievances Ulricans cite when explaining their problems with Sigmarites. @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim} explains this to the Characters if they ask about it.

Reporting to the Graf.name: Reporting to the Graf
Reporting to the Graf.text:
The guard on the palace has been doubled, but all seems peaceful outside. Upon identifying themselves, the party is handed off to a succession of guards, servants, and courtiers before being ushered into the Graf ’s audience chamber. The Graf sits on his throne, flanked by several guards from the Order of the Knights Panther.

When the Characters enter, everyone’s attention is on @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.r4Bd5zWLRdZPaOsj]{High Capitular Werner Stolz}, Middenheim’s most senior priest of Sigmar, who stands before the Graf. Characters passing a Challenging (+0) Perception Test notice that someone has trodden on the hem of his robe, leaving a smear of filth.

‘The Grand Theogonist expresses his concern at recent events. He suggests urgent talks to mend relations between the faiths of Sigmar and Ulric. To that end, he has appointed High Capitular Volkmar Hindenstern as an ambassador extraordinary. The High Capitular wishes to speak to you forthwith regarding proposals the Cult of Sigmar believe will ameliorate tensions in the Empire.’

A moment of silence descends, but before the assembled advisors and ambassadors can respond to Stolz’s announcement, @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} strides across the room and bows to his father. Graf Boris holds up a hand, and the conversation ceases. ‘We shall resume this discussion shortly,’ he says. ‘ You’ — he indicates the @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron}, @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Vieran Thugenheim}, and the Characters — ‘remain where you are, everyone else is dismissed’.

Graf Boris motions the party to sit, and orders a liveried servant to bring refreshments. He wastes no time with preliminaries. First he turns to Heinrich.

‘Baron, it is good to see you returned to us and in the company of the Komission as well. No doubt, you will tell us of your mission, but before I accept your debrief, I want to find out what has befallen my friends here since we last spoke.’ He turns his attention to the Characters. ‘First, I must apologise to you. Clearly the Skaven presented a greater threat than any of us had been willing to admit prior to your investigations. I wish I had paid more heed.’

‘Now we are beset by an infestation of Sigmarites. I’m minded to meet with this High Capitular and find out what the Grand Theogonist has to say, but my fierier subjects say we’re showing weakness by so much as letting them stay in the city. What do you think?’

Characters passing a Challenging (+0) Perception Test notice that both @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} and @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim} goggle in surprise as Graf Boris consults with them so respectfully.

If the Characters have strong opinions on the matter, the Graf hears them out. He responds accordingly to the following topics, if they are raised.

The High Capitular’s Visit

The Graf is interested in the Characters’ opinion of the wisdom of meeting the Sigmarites. Privately he has already decided to arrange a modest palace function tomorrow afternoon at which to receive the High Capitular and hear his proposals, but if the Characters have any suggestions or concerns, he listens to them and at least pretends to take their advice on board.

Karak Skygg

The topic of Karak Skygg is broached by the Graf, if the Characters do not raise it first. If the Characters succeeded in their missions, his is ebullient and congratulatory. If they did not, and northern Ostland has been showered with Warpstone, he is contrite, and says more ought to have been done to support the Characters before it came to this.

Kärzburdgers

If the Characters mention the Kärzburdgers, Graf Boris says that @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.rCdeAWvx9ToE9CDy]{Emmiline von Kärzburdger} recently arrived in Middenheim. She has asked to speak to him regarding the Characters’ actions at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.journals.z5Rjl2Tmbabj1i3b]{Picket}. If the Characters have nice things to say about Emmiline, the Graf asks whether she should be invited to the function he is planning. If not, he sends word that he is too busy with the Sigmarite delegation to meet with her at this time.

Skaven

The Graf is apologetic about failing to appreciate the degree of threat posed by the Skaven. He says he is working together with Middenheim’s Dwarfs to investigate the degree to which they infest the Undercity. If the Characters have any leads to surviving members of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.journals.VQnLCPCECyNBqnOL]{Cult of the Yellow Fang}, he listens seriously. (See @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.journals.xuMYF8PnKeT9XsGz.JournalEntryPage.2l0nR82l4fawlNdL]{Villainous Factions}.)

Nordland

If the Characters report on the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.journals.MopU5CF5WttWo6gS.JournalEntryPage.xPpzTtZKOWVnn7UM#scourge-riders]{Scourge-Riders} or mention the Rocket Crew that attacked the dirigible, the Graf grows grave. He mentions that there have been numerous reports of reaving from Nordland, and that he has asked Baron Nikse to crack down on the rebels.

Wasmeier

No news.

Once the Characters have given their report, the Graf thanks them again for their service and suggests they retire to their rooms in the Templars Arms, or wherever else they might prefer to stay in the city. @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} and @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim} remain in the audience chamber to give their own reports.

About an hour later, a liveried servant arrives at the Characters’ lodgings with an invitation to attend an event at the palace at 7:00 p.m. tomorrow evening. @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular Volkmar} is to be formally welcomed and asked to present his proposals.

Debrief with Schutzmann.name: Debrief with Schutzmann
Debrief with Schutzmann.text:
If the Characters played through The Horned Rat they may decide to approach @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.jBamTcOi8iz3mYxe]{Ulrich Schutzmann}, commander of Middenheim’s Watch. He is at his office in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.Non5YhyYgrHDW6mB]{Square of Martials} during the day. If they visit him, Ulrich is extremely gracious. He seems a little deferential and cautious, a Character passing a Hard (–20) Intuition Test can tell he is anxious. As one of the few open Sigmarites among Middenheim’s high society, Ulrich is feeling increasingly friendless.

‘Thank Sigmar, you are safe. You might have noticed things have become increasingly divided whilst you were away. My best code breakers have been searching through various papers found in the Windhund Haulage basement. With Gottfried Jarmund’s help, I was hoping you could shed more light on them.’

Once @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.jBamTcOi8iz3mYxe]{Ulrich Schutzmann} has the Characters’ attention he asks them the following questions, depending on their previous experience and what he knows of it:

  • There seems to have been a lot of talk amongst members of the Purple Hand in Middenheim about Kastor Lieberung. Do you know who he is?

  • Kastor was expected to deliver a large amount of money about a month ago. Do you know what became of it?

  • He is often mentioned as proposing a consolidation of cult resources, sponsoring Nine Eyes, who will in turn produce a Champion in Shadows. Do you know what this might be about?

  • There seems to be a great deal of confusion as to whether or not the Purple Hand in Middenheim should be subservient to the Purple Hand in Altdorf, or elsewhere, or whether the cults in each city should run their own affairs. Kastor is the only member of the cult who seems to be known to cells in multiple cities. Do you know why this is?

  • How does a cult with no central authority become established in multiple cities, following the same modus operandi?

Middenheimers in Attendance

NameAllegiancesAttitude
Graf @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Boris Todbringer}Middenheim and Ulric (moderate)Whilst he is still a little flabby and uncertain from his period of withdrawal, the Graf is steadily returning to his former confidence and authority.
@UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{'Princess' Katarina Todbringer}Middenheim and Ulric (moderate)Also growing in confidence. Katarina wishes to see war avoided, but also seeks to be taken seriously and shown due respect.
@UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich Todbringer}Middenheim and Ulric (moderate)Bewildered by how much has changed during his absence. Keen to reassert control.
@UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim}Middenheim and Ulric (moderate)Equally bewildered. Keen to show his support for the Todbringers. 
@UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric Emil Valgeir}Ulric (partisan)A fierce defender of Ulrican values and traditions, the new Ar-Ulric wishes to make it clear that he is a very different man to his predecessor.
@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.rCdeAWvx9ToE9CDy]{Emmiline von Kärzbrudger}Sigmar (moderate)Only there if the Characters vouched for her earlier. Emmiline is pleased that she has been shown enough respect to be invited. Slightly paranoid that she and her family are being set up for future humiliation.
@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.actors.f9GN3PQGUp9tjSCT]{Hausmeister Breugal}Middenheim and Ulric (moderate)Careful not to get involved in politics, the Hausmeister’s main concerns are the stage management of the event and to ensure the Graf is treated with due respect.
@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dBIV62DP69lOoUAV#bettie-greenhill-—-head-of-the-kitchen]{Bettie Greenhill}NeutralBettie scuttles between the kitchens and the dining room throughout the event, ensuring that food and drink are always available.

Altdorfers in Attendance

NameAllegiancesAttitude
High Capitular @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar von Hindenstern}Altdorf and Sigmar (partisan)The High Capitular seeks only to serve his Grand Theogonist. A grim man, he is unsuited to social occasions and simply wants to make his proposals and leave.
Graf @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Liepmund Holzkrug}NeutralThe High Lord Ambassador purports to support Altdorf (moderate), but deeply resents the Emperor he purports to serve. A hunter, he is after two goals: war between Middenheim and Altdorf, and his own reputation to remain unblemished.
@UUID[Actor.bddoUxOTF19PyRKm]{Quintus Fassbinder}NeutralA little confused as to why he is there, this unorthodox scholar was selected to advise Liepmund Holzkrug, who seems to want little to do with him. Quintus is rather bored and in need of distraction.
@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Yann Zuntermein}The Purple HandA spy for Altdorf ’s Black Chamber and advisor to Graf Holzkrug. He is keen to observe goings on, but also remains in the shadows. To this end, he has recommended several rather loud personalities to accompany the delegation in the hope that they will demand all the attention.
@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Gravin Luciana von Eckstein}NeutralShe purports support Altdorf (moderate), but is in fact neutral. Descended from Estallian nobility and tired of her life in Altdorf. She is a willing pawn of Altdorf ’s Chancellor Tybalt and a worshipper of Solkan, god of vengeance.
@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.qzV2SdruydGXdMmu]{Baron Ewald von Laue}Altdorf (partisan)A Nordlander who lives in Altdorf and has no love for his native country. Overtly he is here to advise Graf Holzkrug on Nordland politics, but he has also been tasked by Imperial Chamberlain Graf von Bitternach, to gather information to support Nordland’s independence from Middenheim. He is a shameless toady to those more powerful than he is.

At the Palace.name: At the Palace
At the Palace.text:
The event is attended by a small group of diplomats representing Middenheim’s interests, and another group of diplomats representing the interests of groups around the Empire. Servants circulate among the room with drinks and plates of food, but they know not to eavesdrop and guests know not to overindulge.

The room is guarded by a cadre of Knights Panther. The order is sworn to uphold the integrity of the Empire, and so is seen as a neutral presence by most guests. However, the order in Middenheim has had a long history of cooperation with the Todbringers, and those who realise this do not regard them as neutral at all.

The Middenheimers centre on the Graf and his household. They are largely in favour of a moderate solution to the rising tensions, but are willing to be bullish in the face of any ‘Sigmarite nonsense’. However, the new Ar-Ulric, @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Emil Valgeir}, is aggressive in his promotion of Ulrican interests and unwilling to compromise.

The Altdorfers are here to offer two proposals that are, on the face of it, sensible compromises. Whilst the leader of the Altdorf delegation is ostensibly High Capitular @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{Volkmar}; in fact, High Lord Ambassador @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug} has organised the delegation. He is secretly a political enemy of the Emperor’s family, the Holswig-Schliesteins. Graf Holzkrug hopes to achieve his mission, but also wishes to sow distrust during his visit. His team of diplomats have been chosen to cast him in a good light, their own quirks and hang-ups may lead to confusion and upset.

The Characters have earned the respect of Graf Boris. Whilst they might not know it, he respects their opinions. He judges them as uncorrupted by the ambitions of powerful nobles, save maybe for himself. He actively seeks their advice, and whilst certain decisions are inevitable, the Characters should feel that they have been instrumental in the process. Clever diplomacy from the Characters could earn them the respect of attendees and information that might be of use in the future.

19:00 – The Event Commences

The Characters are admitted to the palace’s Great Dining Room. The furniture has been cleared to the sides of the room to encourage guests to mingle. Tables laden with plates of succulent delicacies and flagons of fine wine line one side of the room. A detail of Knights Panther stand guard at the door.

The Middenheim delegation is there when the Characters enter. They greet the Characters and are pleasant and polite, save for @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-pbtt.actors.f9GN3PQGUp9tjSCT]{Breugal}, who finds fault in the slightest breach of etiquette or suitable attire, and @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric Emil}, who is clearly brooding.

The Altdorf delegation arrives about five minutes after the Characters. Graf Holzkrug struts in as if he owns the place, friendly but overbearing. @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Yann Zuntermein} follows, smiling and unctuous, refusing to be drawn beyond preliminary greetings. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Gravin von Ekstein} is coldly polite and looks like she would rather be anywhere else. Baron von Laue is neurotic, a fish out of water who flatters everyone in the hope of making friends. @UUID[Actor.bddoUxOTF19PyRKm]{Quintus Fassbinder} is loudly appreciative of all the new experiences he is having on his first visit to Middenheim. @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{The High Capitular} is a serious man, with almost monosyllabic brevity of speech.

Characters passing an Average (+20) Lore (Reikland) Test or Challenging (+0) Lore (Politics) Test recall that @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug} is a member of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.sVFygKRicWFw6BsT#reikland-council]{Reikland Council} handling the Grand Province’s foreign affairs. With 3 SL or more, they also know that he is the scion of a former Imperial dynasty. On an Easy (+40) Lore (Theology) or Average(+20) Lore (Politics) Test Characters have heard that the @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular} is regarded as stern and serious, but professional. The other guests are such minor figures that no one is likely to know of them.

Whilst the parties mingle the two men with the least in common also seem to be the most alike. On one side of the room Ar-Ulric stands apart, frowning and muttering under his breath; whilst to the other side, @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular Volkmar} matches him glower for glower and pointedly refuses to make small talk.

19:05 – Pleased to meet you, Herr Lieberung

Shortly after the mingling commences the Characters are met by @UUID[Actor.bddoUxOTF19PyRKm]{Quintus Fassbinder}, who is gregarious to the point of mania. How this meeting goes will depend on whether the Lieberung lookalike is still with the party. If the lookalike is there, Fassbinder initially reacts with horror.

‘Quintus Fassbinder at your service, distinguished professor of the — You? But I was told that you had perished! What in Sigmar’s name are you doing here?’ He then grasps the lookalike by the chin and twists their head from side to side in a surprisingly strong grasp. ‘No … no … you aren’t him. He had a sort of Tilean nose, and the eyebrows were less furry. I’m terribly sorry, I mistook you for an old acquaintance. Please excuse me.’

Quintus is embarrassed and crestfallen, but if the name Kastor Lieberung is brought up he becomes excited once again.

‘So you know of Kastor? What a coincidence! Look, now is not the time, but we must talk more about this at some point. I believe we are to make a journey towards the south in one another’s company if all goes well. We can talk then.’

If the lookalike is not in the group, Quintus merely introduces himself.

‘Quintus Fassbinder at your service, distinguished professor of the Altdorf University, and who might you be?’

Quintus is keen to hear about the Characters and their story, particularly if they mention tangling with Chaos cults.

‘ You have suffered brushes with the worshippers of the ruinous gods? But this is my specialist area of study! I must speak to you more about this. This is neither the time nor the place, but I believe we will soon be travelling to Altdorf together. We can talk then.’

If Quitntus is asked how he knows the party will be going to Altdorf, he stutters and stares at his feet, mumbling that he has said too much and spoke out of turn. ‘Things will be made clear soon enough, ignore me.’

19:15 – First Outburst

The Altdorf delegation may consist of nobles and diplomats, but it is as if the delegation’s members were chosen deliberately for their unsuitability — which is precisely the case. @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug} does not fear war between the provinces, he desires it. He is so resentful of the Emperor’s family that he is happy to see the Empire in flames, especially if it humiliates Karl-Franz.

Of course, @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug} is not so reckless as to make his desires known, and the @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular} would not appreciate any diplomatic sabotage. So Holzkrug appears to have put a respectable team of diplomats together, but he knows they have extreme personalities and will no doubt cause a scandal.

The Characters can burnish their own reputations here, justifying them as upstanding and unbiased individuals in the eyes of at least some of the attendees.

The first outburst comes from @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Gravin von Ekstein}. A secret worshipper of the god Solkan, she has become increasingly intolerant and vengeful as a result. Characters who have announced that they are keeping an eye on the Gravin, or @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug}, or @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.dBIV62DP69lOoUAV#bettie-greenhill-—-head-of-the-kitchen]{Bettie Greenhill}, notice on a Hard (–20) Perception Test that the Graf suddenly lurches backwards just as the Halfling passes by with a tray of drinks. Bettie jinks left to avoid the Graf, collides with the Gravin, and spills several glasses of red wine down her sky blue taffeta dress, leaving a noticeable stain.

Whilst this would normally earn Bettie a stern rebuke, the Gravin’s reaction is out of all proportion. She yells at the top of her voice, her Reikland accent inflected with an Estalian lilt, and her refined Altdorf manners replaced with hot Solkanite fire.

Gravin von Ekstein: ‘You noxious little pipsqueak! Is this the way guests are treated in Middenheim? I’ll see you skinned alive you scampering little rat!’

Bettie Greenhill: ‘Dear me, lovey, don’t get angry. I’ll pay for the dress if salt won’t lift the stain out.’

Gravin von Ekstein: ‘Pay with your blood! Graf Boris, I insist you resolve to be rid of this bothersome Halfling as swiftly and permanently as possible! Retribution, I cry! Retribution!’

Baron Heinrich: ‘I’m sure there’s no need, if Chef Greenhill says she can make amends then she will.’

Gravin von Ekstein: ‘Then it’s war between our two cities after all, I tell you, WAR!’

Everyone is shocked, even @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular Volkmar} and @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric Emil}, who had previously been wholly engaged in staring daggers at each other, are taken aback. If a Character announces that they are trying to gauge the reactions of people in the room, they may notice on a Very Hard (–30) Perception Test that @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug’s} face betrays a flicker of satisfaction, before he too adopts a show of surprise.

The Characters have an opportunity to alleviate the situation before other people react. If they make moves to intervene, they find it fairly easy to defuse the situation. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Gravin von Ekstein} realises that she has overstepped her bounds, but as a proud Solkanite she would never admit to wrongdoing. On the other hand, Bettie is terrified that the southern noble will continue to demand her beheading.

Therefore, both parties are ready to cease escalations — provided someone else intervenes. The manner in which Characters get involved may affect how other folks regard them.

NOBLES IN ATTENDANCE

Gravin @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Luciana von Eckstein} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.qzV2SdruydGXdMmu]{Baron Ewald von Laue} are described in more detail in Altdorf: Crown of the Empire, whereas @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.rCdeAWvx9ToE9CDy]{Emmiline von Kärzburdger} is described in The Horned Rat. Whilst they should not need to interact with the Characters if you require profiles for them and do not have either of these books use the information for @UUID[Actor.iDp5L29gbdNcYmGx]{Nobles as described in Knight}.

If the Characters wait and see what other people do, @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} steps in and asks Bettie to go to the kitchen. He then has a quiet word with @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.Mrtalh7JgYNgolzt]{Gravin von Ekstein} and reassures her that the accident was unintentional. She bids him goodbye and returns to her guest room in one of the palace outbuildings.

If Characters accuse @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug} of playing a part in the accident, he flatly denies it.

RESOLVING THE FIRST OUTBURST

Actions by the CharactersEffect
Defuse the situation in such a way that satisfies the honour of Gravin von Ekstein.Add two to the party allegiance score. 
Defuse the situation in an even-handed manner.No effect.
Defuse the situation in such a way that protects the feelings of Bettie Greenhill.Subtract two from the party allegiance score.

19:25 – Second Outburst

The second outburst is made by @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug}. Anyone observing him talking to @UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Thugenheim} hears the conversation, which starts as a measured exchange but soon rises to a crescendo.

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘I am informed at least that you opposed the motion. If only more Altdorfers had been of your opinion.’

Graf Holzkrug: ‘Preceptor you must know I always stand by my emperor in his decisions.’

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘But I’m told that privately you objected?’

Graf Holzkrug: ‘Maybe … maybe not strongly enough. The emperor and his uncle were convinced that the Jungfreuds were swelling their retinues in preparation to rebel though … sigh … they never let me review the evidence that led them to this conclusion.’

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘And since the takeover of Ubersreik no evidence of rebellion has come to light?’

Graf Holzkrug: ‘No. On the contrary! It appears the Jungfreuds had done nothing untoward. By the Hammer! They were loyal! There are those at the palace who refuse to believe it yet, but the JUNGFREUDS WERE LOYAL AND THE TAKEOVER HAS BEEN AN INCALCULABLE BLUNDER!’

@UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Graf Holzkrug} realises too late that he has raised his voice loud enough for the whole @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.SbaXkT2ZupAWRthT]{Middenpalaz} staff to have heard him. He settles down and looks bashful. If a Character announces that they are trying to read his intention they notice on a Very Hard (–30) Intuition Test that his anger seems feigned.

If Characters are interested in discussing the takeover of Ubersreik, @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Holzkrug} happily engages with them, but this time he purports to support the Emperor’s right to depose the Jungfreuds — something other nobles present disagree with. How the Characters respond may affect how they are perceived.

RESOLVING THE SECOND OUTBURST

Opinions voiced by the CharactersEffect
Suggest that Karl-Franz ought to be able to depose nobles he feels may rebel against him.Add two to the party allegiance score. 
Even-handed or silent on the matter.No effect.
Suggest that Karl-Franz stay out of other nobles’ business.Subtract two from the party allegiance score.

19:35 – Third Outburst

The third outburst is more of a toadying whine. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.qzV2SdruydGXdMmu]{Baron von Laue} was once a minor noble of Nordland, but his capricious and craven currying of favour lost him the respect of his peers. He recently decamped to Altdorf, hoping that his obsequious manners would find him allies there. Unfortunately for him, he was assumed to be a patriotic Nordlander, and is now in the pocket of Altdorf nobles who hope to benefit from an independent Nordland.

Now @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.qzV2SdruydGXdMmu]{Baron von Laue} finds himself in Middenheim, who rule Nordland, working on behalf of agents who hope he will inspire revolution in Nordland, when in his heart he knows his fellows in Nordland regard him as a laughing stock. The fact that von Laue tries so hard to be a friend to all that he ends up an enemy to himself is about to take a further twist as Baron Heinrich suspects him of inflaming tensions between Middenheim and Nordland.

Baron Heinrich: ‘Have you been in touch with any of your old friends in Salzenmund since your move to Altdorf?’

Baron von Laue: ‘My good Baron, of course, I have many friends in Salzenmund with whom I carry out warm and extensive correspondences.’

Baron Heinrich: ‘Are you a friend of the Nikses?’

Baron von Laue: ‘Pfft! New money, my Baron. Hardly anyone in Salzenmund pays them great heed.’

Baron Heinrich: ‘The Nikses? To whom the Todbringers are related by marriage and who rule Nordland?

Baron von Laue: ‘The Nikses! Of course! Old family friends, dear Baron, many a cherished evening has been spent watching the ships come in with my good friend Baron … ah … Baron Werther by my side, sharing a bottle of rum.’

The pair continue to talk, but a Character passing an Easy (+40) Intuition Test can tell @UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich} is extremely unimpressed.

Baron Heinrich: ‘What know you of the Gaussers?’

Baron von Laue: ‘Fine fellows, dear Baron! Why I cannot tell the number of times I have enjoyed the hospitality of the celebrated Gausser family.’

Baron Heinrich: ‘You know, recently bandits from Nordland have been claiming to act in their name.’

Baron von Laue: ‘Rotters the lot of them, my Baron. Manann knows each and every Gausser as a traitorous cur!’

Baron Heinrich: ‘I thought you said they were friends of yours?’

Baron von Laue: ‘Never and not so. NO VON LAUE WOULD HAVE ANYTHING TO DO WITH THE REBELLIOUS BENIGHTED GAUSSERS!’

The conversation dies down after this, though if the Characters enquire, they find @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.qzV2SdruydGXdMmu]{Baron von Laue} has no particular knowledge of Nordland’s noble families and simply tells people what he thinks they want to hear. Having been reminded that the Nikses manage affairs in Nordland for Graf Boris, and that the Gaussers defy Middenheim’s rule, he now purports to uphold the sincere belief that the Nikses are fine rulers and the Gaussers traitorous ingrates. If the Characters voice their own ideas it may affect how they are perceived.

RESOLVING THE THIRD OUTBURST

Opinions voiced by the CharactersEffect
Suggest that Nordland’s independence may not be a bad idea.Add two to the party allegiance score. 
Stay out of it.No effect.
Suggest that Nordland be grateful for the patronage of Graf Boris.Subtract two from the party allegiance score.

19:45 – The Propositions

Having watched the antics of the Altdorf delegation with growing disgust the @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular} steps forward and gives a terse report of the two proposals he has been asked to put to the Todbringers. He strides into the centre of the room and strikes the floor with his staff of office.

‘My lords and ladies, now we are introduced I shall deliver my message. His high holiness the Grand Theogonist travels to the Shrine of the Shining Rock, symbol of unity and hope. He beseeches you, Ar-Ulric Emil Valgeir, to meet him, clasp hands in respect and vow to uphold the integrity of our Empire. And to say aloud that the heresy is a lie.’

‘My god is not a god of peace,’ Ar-Ulric replies.

‘Nor mine,’ the High Capitular replies. ‘And if we can stand united against our enemies then our enemies have true cause for woe.’

People in the room seem rather humbled by the @UUID[Actor.RSmsdG8PqbyKnxlL]{High Capitular’s} words, even @UUID[Actor.sn0zk1QV53XMipVw]{Ar-Ulric} broods in silence.

‘Furthermore,’ says the High Capitular, ‘Crown Prince Wolfgang Holswig-Abenhauer extends his hand in marriage to Katarina Todbringer, daughter of the Graf of Middenheim. Now you will excuse me, I have a long journey to Shining Rock ahead. Send your answer before I leave in the morning.’

He leaves without ceremony and the rest of the Altdorf delegation trail out after him. Quintus is last to go, bidding everyone goodbye personally and with bathetic enthusiasm.

Eavesdropping

As well as the subplots there are occasions during the event when one NPC mentions sensitive information to another that the Characters could use as leverage, or as a clue to wider events. In order to overhear such an exchange, Characters must have announced to the GM that they are hovering close to one of the NPCs involved, but not so closely that the NPC would notice them eavesdropping.

Alternatively, if Characters announce at any time that they are looking to see if anything interesting is happening, call for them to make a Challenging (+0) Perception Test to notice the exchange.

In either case the Character must then make a Stealth (Urban) Test opposed by the Perception of the Character they are shadowing (or if they are sidling up to a pair of Characters, the higher Perception of the two). Characters with the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.5KP9sOoLSGvj9EXp]{Beneath Notice} Talent automatically pass this test and hear the whole exchange.

A better way to overhear conversations would be to make use of the Petty Magic spell @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.fmx1OeOsxkGf21wa]{Eavesdrop}, though Characters who are caught casting the spell incur the outrage of the person they are trying to listen to.

Opportunities to eavesdrop come up whenever it suits you as a GM, but in each case there ought to be at least two opportunities for Characters to notice that the NPCs in question are having a private conversation, and move to listen in if they wish.

Graf Boris and Veiran Thugenheim

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘If we’re concerned about sending the right message, we could dig the old Carroburg colours out of the vaults.’

Boris Todbringer: ‘Now that’s an excellent idea. You have my blessing.’

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘I’ll send Sergeant Hortiz for it before we leave.’

Boris Todbringer: ‘Preceptor, best do it yourself. I wouldn’t want word of this reaching the wrong ears.’

Veiran Thugenheim: ‘Ah. Yes. Very good, my lord.’

Veiran and the Graf have decided to present an old war banner, captured from a Reikland regiment in the Age of Wars, as a peace offering. The gift is mildly provocative, as explained later in @UUID[JournalEntry.fgrD3J7lhVYdc7VF.JournalEntryPage.Ip4gsNUFocBJQGmk]{The War Prize}.

Baron Heinrich and Liepmund Holzkrug

Graf Holzkrug: ‘Tensions between Ostland and Talabecland has been simmering for generations, and has more to do with control of Ostland’s forests than the death of Crown Prince Hergard. I wouldn’t blame yourself.’

Heinrich Todbringer: ‘I don’t, we did all we could.’

Graf Holzkrug: ‘Based on the best intelligence Nastassia could gather, no doubt.’

Heinrich Todbringer: ‘My mind must be getting as foggy as Altdorf. I haven’t a clue who you are talking about.’
