The simplest way to utilise the @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} in Empire in Ruins would be to use @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon} as an aspect of the other Daemon. Gideon is a powerful shapeshifting Daemon of Tzeentch, but he is less potent a creature than the Changeling.

In this case the @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} could itself have become compromised, cursed by Tzeentch of impeded through the activity of another Chaos god. In this scenario @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon} is a weak projection of the Changeling, working relatively incognito. The ritual at the end of Empire in Ruins is not just intended to free @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru}, but to restore the Changeling to full power. Its appearance in the @UUID[Scene.RA5QXcxGHPVZnnbf]{Volkshalle} will add even more chaos and confusion to the finale.

The Changeling as Rival to Gideon

Another way the @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} could be employed is as a rival of Gideon. Tzeentch may well be the patron of both Daemons, but this does not mean that they necessarily work towards the same ends. Tzeentch’s plans are so ineffable and labyrinthine that it is plausible that even his Daemonic servants may find themselves pitched against one another in order to serve a greater plan.

As a rival to @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon} the @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} may want to see the summoning of Sheerargetru delayed, subverted, or prevented. There are several ways he might do this.

He may take the shape of one of the crew of the Carroburg, ensuring that the vessel is dogged with problems, leaks, supply shortages, mysterious deaths and other mishaps.

He may take the form of guards or soldiers in the employ of @UUID[Actor.umAaCuMoMplgq6GG]{Marius Lietdorf} or Countess @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle von Liebwitz}. These folk may try to delay the characters by revealing them when they are trying to sneak through or hide in Streissen or Nuln. They may also make wild denunciations, accusing the Characters of having sympathies with Sudenland (to Emmanuelle) or the Alptraums (to Lietdorf ).

He could take the form of @UUID[Actor.XuZtsncLRagDpswg]{Cruzzik Cacklespit} or one of the other leaders of the @UUID[JournalEntry.p6ttZVxrPdkr0BLl]{Madcraw} clan, ensuring that the Goblins put up much stiffer resistance to the Characters as they make their way through the gorge.

The Changeling as an Ally of Gideon

Where the Changeling could make the most direct impact on the adventure is as an assistant to @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon}, making sure that the ritual used to summon @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru} goes off as well as it can. The most direct way the Changeling will try to do this to get the Characters to retrieve corrupt objects during their journey that will help top fortify Sheerargetru when he manifests in the @UUID[Scene.RA5QXcxGHPVZnnbf]{Volkshalle}.

The Changeling gets four chances to influence the Characters in the way during their return journey with the hammer. In each of these occasions the Changeling avoids the Character with Ghal Maraz, and leaves the area quickly if Ghal Maraz is flourished.

In any tavern or club the Characters stop at during the return journey the Changeling manifests as a gambling man called Rudi Böttcher. Rudi looks hangodg and desperate, with wet eyes that seem permanently on the verge of tears.

He tries to engage the players in a game of Red Empress, but he is having a run of bad luck, and soon all he has to play with is an old medal awarded to his grandfather by an Estallian Duke. The medal is gold and bears a magical symbol. It is worth 2 gold crowns if it is pawned. The medal is actually a magical artefact that attracts the winds of magic and adds +1 SL to any successful Channelling Tests the wearer makes.

Benni Shorthill is a travelling Halfling herbalist who passes the Characters on the road or river. He has a touselled thatch of red hair and is missing all his incisors. He offers them a discount on a case containing 6 @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.gxdjLQoQUTYgD6fm]{Healing Draughts}. Normally this would cost 3 gold crowns, but Benni is proud of his new recipe and says the case may be purchased of a single crown. If one of the Characters is injured Benni even demonstrates the efficacy of his potions on them. The Healing Draughts are all effective, but the fifth bottle in the case is filled with Daemonic ichor and is most definitely not good to drink.

At the Wulfshugel the @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} manifests as an aging veteran called Gerd Heideck. Gerd is a bent-backed and bald man with a deeply lined face. His right cheek is a mass of scar tissue and his right eye is missing. ‘Backfiring handgun’ he explains to anyone who asks. He has found an artefact on the hill, a small stone with a spiral diagram etched onto it. ‘You ought to hang on to it’ he tells one of the Characters. ‘These devices were left behind by those who raised the Oghams, it’ll bring you luck.’ The device does indeed bring luck, as the Character who bears it benefits from an additional Fortune Point per session until the manifestation of @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru}.

Vroni Dachdecker is a young pedlar working the roads near Altdorf. She is a short girl with a pronounced limp. She sells arrows, bolts and slingshot bullets. If the Characters need any arrows or bolts, she will sell them a quiver full, decorated with bright blue feathers.

These items are all imbued with ritual significance pertaining to the summoning of a Daemon, and if they are present when @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru} is being summoned they effect the summoning in the following ways.

Item PresentPoints
Magical Medallion+2
Vial of Daemonic Ichor+1
Lucky Sign of the Mystic Spiral+1
Arrows fletched with feathers from a Lord of Change+2

The Changeling as Herald of War.name: The Changeling as Herald of War
The Changeling as Herald of War.text:
The @UUID[Actor.tYpH2H0xZ3odU5L1]{Changeling} may not have any direct part in the events of the adventure whilst still being busy. Throughout many of the Empire’s provinces the servants of Tzeentch are engaged in ensuring that the Turmoil goes ahead as quickly and with as much intensity as possible.

The war has been building for some time, but even so it not easy to break down old alliances, beat plowshares into swords, and deploy armies to the field. Thanks to the efforts of @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.IZVgB7zmTm4rK2yJ]{the Purple Hand} and their co-conspirators in the various Eye cults throughout the Empire the nation is poised to descend into violence far more quickly than an observer might otherwise imagine, but a shapeshifting daemon can really help exacerbate matters.

During the course of Empire in Ruins the Characters may be in the company of many scheming nobles who might drop some evidence that they, or the people around them, have been manipulated by a shapeshifter.

On The Sky Wolf

@UUID[Actor.0Z49f8xUPns5OkTA]{Baron Heinrich}, shortly after picking up the characters in the @UUID[Actor.NWkiPjoS1NuxELak]{Sky Wolf}: ‘It had all been going so well. I had just about convinced Hans-Hals von Tasseninck that the Krieglitzes were sincere in their desire to build brides and hold a thorough inquiry into the death of the Crown Prince. I had him ready to call for a stop to all the border disputes and even punish any of his vassals who refused to refrain from further violence. Then, out of nowhere, Gustav von Krieglitz himself stormed into the chamber, grabbed the brim of von Tasseninck’s hat and yanked it down over his face, screaming all the while about the wages of slander. Really put an end to any hope of a constructive outcome. I did all I could to calm Hans-Hals, and then went off to give Gunther a piece of my mind, but he denied he had so much put a hand on the other man, or even entered the chamber. But as Verena is my witness I saw him with my own eyes.’

In Middenheim

@UUID[Actor.LzkGSosXU59kwBIV]{Veiran Thugenheim}, to a fellow Middenheimer at the reception in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-middenheim.journals.PuIrlGBOjxuWpK3P.JournalEntryPage.SbaXkT2ZupAWRthT]{Middenpalaz}, and only if the Character listening in is able to successfully eavesdrop: ‘The Baron’s informants are among the best in the business but if this Gausser fellow is able to act as he seems to be acting, he must have information coming to him constantly and accurately. Several times we have sent out a squadron of Knights to intercept reivers from Nordland, and they evade capture every time. They are even able to work around our squadrons and lay waste to farms and villages whilst we chase after shadows.’

At the Military Parade

Characters may be able to eavesdrop on the following conversation be tween the Emperor’s Double and Immanuel-Ferrand:

The Emperor’s Double: ‘It’s an impressive turnout, but I can’t help feeling we are a little short on men.’

Immanuel-Ferrand: ‘A great many of the city’s troops are still engaged in supressing the situation in Ubersreik your majesty, and a number of knightly orders have declined to attend as they are sworn to defy Beastmen and Goblins, foes they claim are massing in ever greater number in the Reikwald.’

The Emperor’s Double: ‘That may be, but still I had thought to see more troops arrayed from the wider Reikland. Where’s the Grunberg contingent and … what’s his name … the Graf of Bogenhafen?’

Immanuel-Ferrand: ‘Von Saponatheim? In the west! Near Helmgart.’

The Emperor’s Double: ‘Well what in Sigmar’s name is he doing there? We’re not at war with Bretonnia are we?’

Immanule-Ferrand: ‘Between you and I, we may well be yet. He claims to be in possession of intelligence suggesting the Duke of Pavarron has come to a deal with the monstrosities of Blood Keep and they plan to combine in alliance.’

The Emperor’s Double: ‘By all of the gods. What utter piffle!’

In Averland and Nuln

Virtually anywhere the Characters stop on their journey there will be similar tales. Military forces happen to be directed through uncannily precise, or terribly misleading, information, into being just where they need to be, or don’t need to be, in order to cause the war the develop much faster and more fiercely than it otherwise might. Regiments on manoeuvres find themselves arriving at villages at the same time as raiders poised to pounce on them, wagon trains are ambushed by Beastmen or Goblins, hostilities are declared between nobles before they even realise that they had swollen their fighting retinues to massive capacities.

In the aftermath of Empire in Ruins the Characters may decide to chase these stories down, and in many cases they will find that the captains, quartermasters and noble lords who fought the war cannot account for strokes of good fortune, ill luck or exacerbating circumstances that contributed to the conflict.

But What If ... ?.name: But What If ... ?
But What If ... ?.text:
What if the Characters prevent that final battle with @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru}? Far from a thrilling conclusion, the ending could feel anticlimactic. In this chapter, we take a closer look at the alternative outcomes mentioned in Empire in Ruins (see @UUID[JournalEntry.DxTPhw2YhWpPVo1c.JournalEntryPage.k6XiWJz5E4noCgFY]{Aftermath and ... Rewards?}) — how you can integrate them into the story, what the near-future of the Empire might be, and present an adventure suggestion worthy of powerful characters. Each table’s campaign is different, however, so use these suggestions as inspirations for your own alternate endings.

Yann Zuntermein - The Spider In His Web

A master spy, @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} may be a Chaos cultist, but he is not stupid. After the events of Power Behind The Throne and The Horned Rat, his informants alert him to the Characters’ growing significance. Meeting them at @UUID[JournalEntry.02qjJrwtrBb6N1H7]{Shining Rock} and noting how they reacted to the attempted assassination of @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina}, he acknowledges them as resourceful figures and, therefore, as possible threats to his plan. If he is wily, they could be potentially useful tools.

How Zuntermein Wins

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein’s} plot entails the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince}, well-groomed by his @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes tutors}, first becoming Prince Regent for the ailing Emperor and then ascending to the throne in his own right.

However, three dangers hover over his plans: @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon}, @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} and the party. First, he suspects Gideon of having his own agenda and that recovering Ghal Maraz is crucial to it. Second, Wasmeier schemes to replace him atop the Altdorf Purple Hand. He could wreck everything. Lastly, the Characters are far too capable for @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein’s} comfort.

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} must prevent the recovery of the Hammer in order to succeed. While the attempt to steal it in Altdorf (@UUID[JournalEntry.DxTPhw2YhWpPVo1c.JournalEntryPage.dHcV3DSWkeeAKu2I#optional-encounter:-zuntermeins-last-grasp]{Zuntermein's Last Grasp}) represents a last, desperate effort, he does have a card to play earlier — @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier}.

Once it becomes clear that a mission to recover @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.eE8H6wRoq0GGpWR8]{Ghal Maraz} is underway, @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} plants information through intermediaries that @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} has been sighted in Altdorf and that he was behind the assassination attempt. Zuntermein himself never appears, though clever investigative work by the Characters should uncover a trail back to him.

Following @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein’s} clues, the Characters find the safehouse in which @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} hides — as well as a faked message identifying @UUID[Actor.bddoUxOTF19PyRKm]{Quintus Fassbinder} as a Purple Hand agent. Written in the same cipher they encountered in Middenheim, it accuses him of conducting research for the cult, something others would be all too willing to believe. With Wasmeier eliminated and Fassbinder discredited, the quest for the Hammer never occurs, the summoning never takes place, and Yann Zuntermein wins.

The Empire Under Zuntermein

@UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} first must consolidate power. If the Characters have not figured out his scheme, then they can still be useful. Soon after the events of Empire in Ruins, the Emperor’s condition worsens as the Purple Hand’s ‘doctor’ continues poisoning him. Zuntermein, manipulating @UUID[Actor.BcGALPPubww6hPnQ]{Liepmund Holzkrug}, has the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.sVFygKRicWFw6BsT#reikland-council]{Reikland Council} declare @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince Wolfgang} Prince-Regent to rule in Karl-Franz’s name as both Grand Prince and Emperor. Wolfgang, under Zuntermein’s influence, takes on the Characters as ‘trusted agents’. Soon, they uncover ‘evidence’ — planted by Zuntermein — implicating Holzkrug in a plot to seize the throne, aided by Else Barnhelm of the Schattenkabinett and General Erik Hoffman of the Palisades. (see @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.W4LFOIduFZoqSNsN.JournalEntryPage.e1vvDKWEn2EYw0gZ]{The Black Chamber}). With these rivals eliminated, the new Prince-Regent ‘reforms’ the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.W4LFOIduFZoqSNsN.JournalEntryPage.e1vvDKWEn2EYw0gZ]{Black Chamber}, making Zuntermein its head and giving him a seat on the Reikland Council, where he becomes de facto prime minister.

Soon, the Palace announces that the ailments of Luitpold, Prince of Altdorf, have grown worse. He is leaving to ‘take the cure’ at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives2.journals.NdCkjAamdihWdQqA]{Great Hospice}, and his mother, the @UUID[Actor.YNXGP1kG2aD47HIP]{Lady Maria-Luise}, will join him to see to his care, while the Prince-Regent oversees the Principality of Altdorf. Thanks to a generous gift from Wolfgang to the hospice for their perpetual upkeep, @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} is confident that neither will cause him problems.

Now secure, @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} implements the Purple Hand’s grand design — ‘reforms’ that break down the pillars of the Empire, weakening it against Chaos. In Reikland, Wolfgang frees all towns from any feudal obligations, leading to outrage among the nobility and joy among the burghers. An Imperial decree suppresses the Order of the Silver Hammer as an enemy of ‘free thought’, eliminates licenses for wizards, and reaffirms the mutant decree. Sigmar’s cult fractures as the Arch-Lectors in Nuln and Talabheim defy orders to obey the new edicts.

While implemented in Reikland, across the Empire the new decrees meet strong resistance in the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-eis.journals.Zt9cBtaoKEL2kjPF.JournalEntryPage.Epef0dqTOuXpTAZ6#the-prime-estates]{Prime Estates} Some grand provinces simply ignore them, while others declare them ‘null and void’ and punish anyone who tries to implement them. A meeting of the Electoral Council the next year to settle matters fails utterly, with @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} declaring the north’s secession and Grand @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} of Nuln proclaiming neutrality. A civil war that lasts years then ravages the Empire.

Agents of Nuln

While she has declared neutrality in the continuing strife, @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Emmanuelle Liebwitz} has not been sitting idle as the Empire collapses around her. Aware more than most of what is really going on, she has laid plans for an uprising that would restore the Holswig-Schliesteins and eliminate @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Yann Zuntermein}. However, to succeed she needs a legitimate claimant, and the only one is Karl-Franz’s son, Prince Luitpold, currently at the Grand Hospice with his sister and their mother, who is also Emmanuelle’s dearest friend.

She thus has to rescue Luitpold and his family. In need of deniable agents and recalling the Characters, Emmanuelle contacts them through intermediaries with an offer: rescue @UUID[Actor.YNXGP1kG2aD47HIP]{Maria-Luise} and her family from the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives2.journals.NdCkjAamdihWdQqA]{Great Hospice} and get them to Nuln in return for noble titles and estates.

The task is not easy. @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} has replaced many on the staff at the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives2.journals.NdCkjAamdihWdQqA]{Great Hospice} with Spionwerber operatives and stationed a ‘reliable’ unit of Reiksguard cavalry nearby as an ‘honour guard’. The Grand Countess also insists on minimal bloodshed — if her agents were to harm any of the Shallyan priestesses there, the political repercussions would be disastrous.

The mission is thus not just extraction, but also a chase, as the Characters evade @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein’s} minions, not to mention hostile local powers. Perhaps their route takes them through Marienburg to the sea, or across the mountain passes and through the Dwarfholds of the Grey Mountains, to Bretonnia, whence they make their way to Tilea and reach Nuln weeks later by way of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-archives1.journals.S1ONBYW4uxw9POV8.JournalEntryPage.jMPCfpAkxavtt9Ix#kreutzhofen]{Alimento} tunnel.

Wasmeier's Revenge.name: Wasmeier's Revenge
Wasmeier's Revenge.text:
Once the head of the Middenheim Purple Hand, Karl-Heinz Wasmeier has fallen far, reduced to a fugitive seeking sanctuary from the cult in Altdorf. But he has plans, and the presence of the Characters gives him the chance to fulfil them… as well as gain revenge.

How Wasmeier Wins and How the Characters Can Help

@UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} wishes to eliminate @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} and assume control of the Purple Hand, taking control of Zuntermein’s schemes and ‘doing them right’. But, he needs to defeat his rival without alerting Zuntermein and destroying the cult. While not fully aware of Gideon’s plans, Zuntermein’s opposition to the Characters’ mission to retrieve @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-empire-ruins.items.eE8H6wRoq0GGpWR8]{Ghal Maraz} gives him an attractive opportunity to use one set of enemies to destroy another.

His plans commence after the Characters’ arrival in Altdorf. After the attempt on @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina’s} life, @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} through pawns drops hints warning of treason within the Black Chamber and around Wolfgang. At the emergency Electoral conclave (@UUID[JournalEntry.mAUuZ2hUO5TrG30w]{Chapter 7}), a cultist loyal to Wasmeier on the Palace staff slips a note in a Character’s food or their pocket alerting them to a meeting of ‘conspirators and cultists’ taking place that night near the university.

The note is genuine. That night is one of ritual significance for the Purple Hand, and @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} is conducting the ceremony, one which Wasmeier misses due to ‘sudden illness’. If the Characters raid the meeting, Zuntermein is exposed, if not killed outright. @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} then assumes command of the Purple Hand.

Regardless of how the Characters take out @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein}, there is still the problem of the summoning; its success would ruin @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier’s} plans. Though he does not know the full picture, Wasmeier knows that someone ordered the replacement of the Reiksguard at the Reliquary with cultists; he assumes this is a crucial part of whatever Zuntermein is planning. He has orders forged that once again change the guard, this time replacing the cultists at the last minute with real, loyal Reiksguard Knights. With this switch, the Hammer does not vanish through the trap door and the sacrifice of the @UUID[Actor.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Grand Theogonist} and @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} do not take place.

The summoning fails, and @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} wins.

Crumbling Empire

Though he has won, @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Karl-Heinz Wasmeier} does not have @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Yann Zuntermein’s} skills and resources. He does not control the Black Chamber, nor even the Spionwerber. He does not gain a seat on the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.sVFygKRicWFw6BsT#reikland-council]{Reikland Council}, so cannot dictate the direction of the Empire’s wealthiest province. Though his plans are large, his means are limited, and his need for revenge against the Characters warps his judgement.

But @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} does have some strings to pull and is still an experienced conspirator. If at least three of the @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} survived, then Wasmeier retains the cult’s influence over the Crown Prince’s education. If any were eliminated by the Characters, he finds replacement tutors with impeccable credentials, thus only briefly delaying matters. Regardless, under an assumed name he takes the place of the Law Tutor, giving him direct access to Wolfgang. The poisoning of the Emperor continues, which leads to the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} becoming Prince Regent. If the Characters uncover the doctor’s plot, Wasmeier’s plans are only inconvenienced; the damage done in the Emperor’s name has severely weakened his standing with the Electors.

Through the influence of the Nine Eyes, he persuades @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Wolfgang} to ‘reform’ Reikland’s judiciary. An Imperial decree establishes a ‘Reikland High Court,’ with authority to appoint all judges and hear all cases in the Grand Province, as well as the authority to revoke any local laws ‘for the sake of uniform justice’. A further decree grants this court authority throughout the Empire. The Chief Judge of this new tribunal is, of course, @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Karl-Heinz Wasmeier}, the Crown Prince’s trusted adviser.

The reaction is furious. The nobility rails against having their ‘ancient privileges’ usurped, freistadts resist losing rights they had just won, and the cults are outraged at being subject to secular law. Even the age-old friendship with the Dwarfs fractures, as the new High Court rules all Dwarfs within the bounds of the Empire are subject to Imperial law, not that of the Dwarf Empire, breaking longstanding treaties.

The breakup of the Empire is even worse than under @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein}. @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} declares himself ‘Wolf Emperor’ as Middenheim and the north secede, while Grand @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} has herself crowned Empress, forming a breakaway Empire with Stirland and Ostermark. The other Grand Provinces choose sides, with only distant Ostland remaining loyal to Altdorf, and even some internal provinces rebel against their Electors, subtly influenced by @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier’s} agents. The control of the Colleges of Magic breaks down, as some wizards escape the new regime to seek patronage and protection from other Electors.

Foreign enemies see their chance, too. The Duke of Parravon begins a sixth war, intending to annex Ubersreik and the Vorbergland. Marienburg demands extensive concessions to supply anyone with needed funds. Greenskins raid from the Black Mountains, and the new Southern Empire has its hands full with both an Orc invasion from Black Fire Pass and the civil war. The chaos lasts for decades.

Upheaval in Ubersreik

Though busy transforming the Empire, @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} has not forgotten the Characters. In fact, he is obsessed with revenge. The perilous situation in @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.icaZcokQLawViHCq]{Ubersreik} gives him the opportunity to exact it

The Characters likely have had to flee Altdorf as Wasmeier gained greater and greater control. Perhaps they went to join @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} in Middenheim, or the @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Grand Countess in Nuln}. Regardless, at their host’s court they find a surprising guest: Leopold von Jungfreud. He had been hiding in Averheim, but had to flee again because of the turmoil there. The remaining von Jungfreuds are either arrested or dead, making Leopold the legitimate heir to the Duchy of Black Rock, the ancestral seat now under Altdorf’s control

News has filtered back from @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.icaZcokQLawViHCq]{Ubersreik} that anger at the new laws has already led to riots, and that the burghers are willing to welcome the von Jungfreuds back. They offer to rise against Altdorf, but only if Leopold comes to lead them. The Elector is interested in anything that will weaken the Prince Regent. Emmanuelle, in particular, would give Ubersreik her protection in return for the von Jungfreuds swearing loyalty to her

It is a trap. While anti-Altdorf sentiment is genuine, cultist spies in @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier’s} service infiltrated the rebel groups and planted the idea of rebellion, knowing that the Characters would likely be the ones sent. The plan is to arrest them at a meeting with the ‘rebels’ where final arrangements were to be made. Unable to resist, Wasmeier himself will lead the raid

If they escape, the Characters have the opportunity to do two things at once — free @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.icaZcokQLawViHCq]{Ubersreik} from Altdorf’s clutches and finally kill @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Karl-Heinz Wasmeier

Lieberung Wins (Posthumously).name: Lieberung Wins (Posthumously)
Lieberung Wins (Posthumously).text:
Though long dead by this point, Kastor Lieberung’s plans could still bear fruit, leading to the bleakest of all futures.

Kastor Victorious

For Lieberung’s plan to succeed, all the others have to fail. While the @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} must survive to complete their work. Ghal Maraz, on the other hand, is irrelevant.

Ironically, the Characters are in the best position to make this happen, however unwittingly. While there are opportunities in Empire in Ruins for the Characters to expose and neutralise both @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} and @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier}, the summoning poses more difficulties. Delivering Ghal Maraz sets the final steps of @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon’s} plan in motion. Even @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru’s} defeat means Lieberung has lost, for his summoning costs the Crown Prince’s life.

If Kastor Liberung’s double has survived, one of the @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} realises that this is not their leader, but still someone who may be useful. Similar to the @UUID[.2zey0gB2ZOcmx4XM]{‘Wasmeier wins’} scenario, this person has learned of the replacement of the Reiksguard, something not part of the plan. Suspecting a double-cross, the cultist pretends to be an innocent scholar who has only just learned the truth. They inform the Character of the substitutions and, having heard of their ‘great exploits’, begs them to do something. However the Characters deal with the problem, eliminating the fake honour guard and somehow preventing @UUID[Actor.6vITnrER3XMTsMGS]{Yorri’s} death means no summoning.

If @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} and @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} have also been dealt with, then the late Kastor Lieberung wins.

Lieberung's Fruit: The Chaos Emperor

In the event of a Lieberung victory, the Turmoil, if it occurs at all, ends quickly. Wisely advised by his tutors and becoming an inspirational leader, Wolfgang quickly eclipses his ailing uncle as de facto ruler of the Empire, if not Emperor in his own right. Moving more slowly than either @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} or @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} would, he first appeases @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} by finding those who planned the assassination of @UUID[Actor.PrkWVIr7Go4u1QWp]{Katarina} and executing them. He mediates between the cults of Sigmar and Ulric, brokering peace between them. He implements reforms to benefit burghers and peasants in Reikland, but only suggests them elsewhere. They become so popular, however, that the other Electors cannot resist. Finally, at a formal electoral conclave, he proposes changes to the structure of the Empire itself, giving Graf Boris and Grand @UUID[Actor.CcqiAghkzgp9u1In]{Countess Emmanuelle} what they wanted, and convincing the others to acquiesce. With the restoration of peace and prosperity, it seems a golden age has begun.

Appearances, however, are deceiving. After a few years @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Wolfgang}, who has replaced most key members of the government with his @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} advisers, announces he is leaving on a pilgrimage to seek the counsel of the gods. In truth, he ventures to the Silver Tower, where he becomes the pupil of the Chaos Sorcerer, Engrim van Horstmann. Returning after three years, Wolfgang, looking and sounding the same, is now the @UUID[Actor.KnN3dPkIPFUBgByl]{Champion in Shadows}, Tzeentch’s greatest servant.

He decrees new reforms to sweep away ‘old, stifling ways’, proclaiming toleration for all religions, including Chaos cults. When the hierarchies of Sigmar and Ulric object, they die in mysterious fires that ravage their chief temples. Magic is deregulated in the name of ‘free inquiry’, prompting the Supreme Patriarch to protest directly to @UUID[Actor.KnN3dPkIPFUBgByl]{Wolfgang}. According to rumour, having once entered the Palace, he never came out. Though some Electors rise in revolt, they are crushed by the preternatural power of the new Emperor’s armies.

Within a few years, the Empire becomes a place of nightmare. The ancient order is cast down, Chaos openly walks the streets, and people live in utter misery under the Chaos Emperor.

Mission to Ulthuan

Months after @UUID[Actor.KnN3dPkIPFUBgByl]{Wolfgang} crushes the last rebellions, the Characters find themselves summoned to a small village near Middenheim. There they meet old acquaintances — @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.ZVVaOEUN9ArYrYnM]{Janna Eberhauer}, now High Wizard of Middenland, and a badly scarred @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.wkR7O1KYE9qaXntF]{Thyrus Gormann}, former Supreme Patriarch of the Colleges of Magic, now in hiding and hunted by the Emperor’s spies.

Having barely survived and escaped his battle with @UUID[Actor.KnN3dPkIPFUBgByl]{Wolfgang}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.wkR7O1KYE9qaXntF]{Gormann} has spent the intervening months re-establishing contact with those still willing to fight back. Realising they need far more powerful magic to defeat the Champion in Shadows, they came to a conclusion — seek aid from the Elves, as was done in the time of Magnus the Pious. Only then would a rebellion have a chance of succeeding.

But the Elves withdrew from the Empire at the rise of Wolfgang. So, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.wkR7O1KYE9qaXntF]{Gormann} and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.ZVVaOEUN9ArYrYnM]{Eberhauer} want the Characters to carry out this mission to Ulthuan. A boat, navigator, and crew await them in Marienburg, but they have to get into the city and then out to sea, while avoiding Wolfgang’s agents and the minions of Jaan van de Kuypers. Head of the most powerful of the Ten, the families that control Marienburg, van de Kuypers has profited immensely from his dealings with Wolfgang and will stop at nothing to protect his interests.

In Ulthuan, the Characters find their reception chilly at best, most at the court in Saphery having written the Old World off as lost. Though the Phoenix King refuses to provide an army, with deft diplomacy they can convince Teclis and @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.EmhvOkkzAir6pzCB.JournalEntryPage.vI5JjfDoKBO3LTl5]{Anurion the Green} of the need to defeat Wolfgang and win their agreement to help.

Getting to the Empire is the problem. Wolfgang’s spies are seemingly everywhere, and neither wizard can use his magic, for fear of revealing their presence too soon. It is up to the Characters to figure out the route to Middenheim, where @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.actors.wkR7O1KYE9qaXntF]{Gormann}, @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-horned-rat.actors.ZVVaOEUN9ArYrYnM]{Eberhauer}, and the @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf} await.

Perhaps through Nordland’s minor ports, perhaps across Norsca and Kislev to arrive from the east, the way home will be fraught with peril no matter what. If they succeed, however, the Graf raises the banner of rebellion and the battle for the Empire begins.

The Characters Triumphant.name: The Characters Triumphant
The Characters Triumphant.text:
But what if, in the end, the Characters foil everyone’s plans?

Not Likely, But How Could This Happen

With all the dangers the Characters face, with all the foes, the odds are heavily against them winning total victory. It is possible, though everything has to come together exactly right.

They must stop the summoning. Defeating @UUID[Actor.BUUxBxaUaB6CNjA2]{Sheerargetru} is not enough, for it almost certainly means the @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Crown Prince} or the Emperor — or both — died to bring forth the daemon. Even protecting them only means that other, albeit imperfect, vessels such as @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} or the @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} would be used instead. One means would be to prevent the Hammer from falling into @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon’s} hands, perhaps by discovering the trap door to the wine cellar from the Reliquary. This would lead to the arrest, interrogation, and confession of @UUID[Actor.x2cF45W4cU4QQW8v]{Ermine Liebwitz}. Thus warned, the authorities move the ceremony to the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-altdorf.journals.cDOlXEpTvnuaOJ0P.JournalEntryPage.TwV8JKaTUnfo3ipT]{Grand Cathedral of Sigmar}, where it goes off without a hitch, the presence of the Hammer preventing a summoning.

They must also stymie @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein}. If he is killed following his attempts to direct his spies to kill the Characters, his threat is over. They could also expose him at any time after meeting him at @UUID[JournalEntry.02qjJrwtrBb6N1H7]{Shining Rock}. They may learn of his machinations through uncovering the plot to poison the Emperor, or discovery of the truth about the Nine Eyes could lead back to him. Confident and arrogant, Zuntermein has discounted any threat from @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier}. If the Characters capture Wasmeier, he could trade what he knows of Zuntermein in return for leniency.

Stopping @UUID[Actor.lYEKyCpaihHON6Gz]{Wasmeier} is the easiest to accomplish. Given their experiences in Middenheim, the Characters may kill him on sight. It is also likely that his unhinged rage at the Characters leads him to attack them, again leading to his death. And @UUID[Actor.Z9wyqpwFr4jnPHTP]{Zuntermein} himself may set him up to distract the Characters, should they be getting close to the truth about the Spionwerber chief.

The @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} tutors are key to Kastor Lieberung’s plans. Killing or exposing them ends their influence over @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Wolfgang}. Convincing Wolfgang of the truth could be hard, but, if they save Karl-Franz and present the evidence to him, he would order the arrest of the tutors and Wolfgang’s ‘re-education’ by the Cult of Sigmar.

If all these pieces fall into place, then the Characters win.

An Empire Rebornn… Sort Of

Although safe from the schemes of a daemon, a master spy, a sorcerer, and a dead man, the Empire remains badly damaged and faces a shaky future. At the top, trust has broken down almost completely in Karl-Franz as Emperor and Grand Prince. Revealing that he was poisoned and controlled by a Chaos cult does little to restore good relations, while the exposure of the @UUID[Actor.b6bu4oI4eRL4abkS]{Nine Eyes} plot makes @UUID[Actor.3GcQxRuIm1MgoAMF]{Wolfgang} unacceptable to the other Electors as Crown Prince.

The Grand Provinces themselves are in upheaval. Independence movements roil Nordland; Ostland and Talabecland remain at war; Nuln edges closer to seizing Sudenland; and the grandees of Reikland fear they could be the ‘next Ubersreik’. Meanwhile, violence continues to break out between the cults of Ulric and Sigmar as rumours spread among Ulricans that the cult of Sigmar consorts with Chaos.

To prevent all-out civil war, Karl-Franz calls another Electoral Conference, and this one succeeds. In the greatest reorganisation since Magnus the Pious, Hochland, Nordland, and Ostermark become Electoral Provinces. To compensate their former rulers, Middenland once again joins Middenheim, with @UUID[Actor.czIY275tUC4VGDWp]{Graf Boris} ruling both. Similarly, Talabheim becomes part of Talabecland upon the marriage of Elise Krieglitz-Untern to Helmut Feuerbach, and Nuln absorbs Sudenland to form the Grand Province of Wissenland. The former ruling families are either deposed — the Krieglitzes, Toppenheimers, Bildhofens, and Alptraums — or replaced upon their extinction, as with the Tassenincks.

To stabilise his rule, Karl-Franz marries @UUID[Actor.YNXGP1kG2aD47HIP]{Maria-Luise} and names their daughter, Alia, as Heir, her education overseen by a committee, including the cults of Sigmar, Ulric, and Verena. The former Crown Prince is named Prince of Vorbergland, which title and estates he can assume once he completes his re-education. Karl-Franz confirms Ubersreik as a freistadt, but compensates the von Jungfreuds.

Though spared the worst, the Empire remains in a delicate state. Foreign enemies look to take advantage of its weakness, resentful losers scheme to get back what was once theirs, while ever in the shadows lurk the Purple Hand and other cults, plotting to turn the Empire into a realm of Chaos.

Long Live the von Wittgendorfs!

Though the Empire is at relative peace, problems remain to test the Characters. Having defeated all the myriad plots and saved Karl-Franz, one of the Characters — the Kastor Lieberung double, if he still lives — is made a baron and receives the estates and castle of the late Wittgenstein family, along with a purse of 20,000 GCs. It is up to them, however, to restore the land and make it profitable. Neighbouring nobles may resent these parvenus, even if they are heroes. While private war is frowned upon in the wake of the Turmoil, there are other ways to take what someone else has, especially if they begin to make the area desirable again.

Imperial politics aside, the long, dark rule of the Wittgenstein family left its mark on the Characters’ new holding. Many secrets may remain in the ruins of the old castle, and perhaps the Skaven have not lost interest in finding them. Many of the Wittgensteins were mutants themselves, and their province became known among the Tainted as a welcoming place. Do the new lords cleanse it with fire, or have their experiences softened their hearts to at least some of those afflicted? And what if jealous rivals pass rumours of their tolerance back to the Witch Hunters?

The Siege of Diesdorf.name: The Siege of Diesdorf
The Siege of Diesdorf.text:
The cult of the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{Red Crown} has decided that recent events across the Empire herald their coming victory. The news that Ghal Maraz was a fake was seen as the sign that signalled the rise of the cult. They have been gathering their forces for years, preparing mutants and Beastmen for this day. They have decided to attack the Reikland town of @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf} with the intention of raiding the garrison armoury and magazine. A force over four thousand strong is answering the call, burning villages and farms as they come. Once they have taken Diesdorf, they intend to march on Altdorf to gather more warriors. Part of their plan was to have Red Crown cultists take control of the town and open the gates to them. However, this coup failed they are ready for a full assault.

When the Characters arrive at @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf}, they are asked to join the town council to prepare for and lead the defence of Diesdorf. The other council members are unprepared to do so and will unintentionally bring ruin upon the town should the Characters refuse. As @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{the Red Crown} horde approaches, the Characters are asked to make decisions about the town’s defence: strengthening the walls, allocating resources, and dealing with fearful citizens with their — often petty — concerns. The Characters’ actions decide whether Diesdorf stands or falls.

Running this Scenario

The focus of this scenario is a series of decisions made by the @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#the-remains-of-the-council]{Diesdorf Town Council} in the days before the town is attacked by a force of Beastmen and mutants. The Characters, heroes of the Empire by this point, are trusted to advise the council, and their decisions will impact Diesdorf ’s future, and perhaps the future of Altdorf itself.

Unlike other scenarios where the focus is on investigation or confronting enemies, here problems come to the Characters. Whilst interacting with other councillors is necessary, the degree to which the Characters explore Diesdorf is up to them; the town is only briefly described with an emphasis on its strategic value.

This scenario could be set in any small town in the Empire under threat from an oncoming horde of Chaos creatures. It could even be adapted so that the approaching enemies are Orc and Goblin raiders or Dark Elf corsairs, who would make similar cruel demands and incite panic in the forlorn townsfolk.

As the GM, it is important to work out how the council’s decisions affect the integrity of the town’s defence, why petitioners to the council are concerned about the issues they raise, and why the other council members vote the way they do.

The dilemmas themselves are more important than the reasons they are raised, but give some thought to them just in case the Characters ask questions. Be prepared to improvise if the Characters do explore the town — they may hear rumours that foreshadow upcoming decisions or spot opportunities to improve Diesdorf ’s defences.

If the Characters are inclined to focus on the town rather than the council meetings, @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain Theocritus von Hayek} can pressure them to remain at the @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#diesdorf-military-college]{Diesdorf Military College} for their own safety. If they ignore him, an assassination attempt by @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P.JournalEntryPage.M5pnsRFFdFH7Obkt]{Red Crown cultists} who remain in the town could help persuade the Characters to keep their heads down.

Recent Events in Diesdorf and Its Surrounds

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{The Red Crown} has been gathering its force for weeks. They have attacked small military patrols and travellers, and more recently started to raid farms and small homesteads. Reports have been sent to @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.V6tkgQ9A2skppjyl]{Altdorf}, @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf}, and other local towns, but nothing has been done.

@UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{The Red Crown’s} army approaches a weakened @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf}. Two of the Military College’s companies have been deployed to Altdorf to support troops that have moved to @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.journals.ozE2DMCMK64eE5pD.JournalEntryPage.icaZcokQLawViHCq]{Ubersreik} and the border between Reikland and Middenland. Yesterday, the cult activated their followers in the town. @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P.JournalEntryPage.M5pnsRFFdFH7Obkt]{Red Crown cultists}, led by council member and Grandmaster Detlef Rotlander of the Blacksmiths’ Guild, attempted to seize control of the town. They tried to assassinate the entire council to sow confusion and place some of their own into power. The baronet and three members of the council, along with senior college officers, were killed. Rotlander is currently on the run.

The senior military officer, @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain Theocritus von Hayek}, believes there is a good chance that @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf} will be attacked directly and is preparing the town. With refugees seeking safety and news of the gathering horde and turmoil elsewhere in the Empire, the population is scared and near panic.

The Road to Diesdorf

With Empire in Ruins in mind, the Characters pass @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf} as they travel to @UUID[JournalEntry.ScPlX4AOyUTa2LKm]{Black Fire Pass} from Altdorf, and again on their return journey.

A contributing factor to the assault on @UUID[Scene.a9kUZhvME0E6VL03]{Diesdorf}, and the Characters needing to stop there, is @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon}. If the Characters are making good time and need to be delayed to suit Gideon’s favoured date of the 9th of Brauzeit, he could divert them to look into the state of the town. He may have seeded word of the Characters’ arrival (rumours that a young man with a page-boy haircut extolling their abilities could be overheard). He could even be in communication with the horde’s leaders, advising them to delay their attack to further delay the Characters. To @UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon}, even a sizable Chaos army is only a pawn to be used to enable a more satisfactory summoning.

@UUID[Actor.IvvkdVTJzutEsrlX]{Gideon} can still ultimately be behind the horde even if the Characters do not need to be delayed. His plans to tip the Empire into Chaos require that troops be drawn from the large cities, particularly Altdorf, so he has been encouraging cults like the @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{Red Crown} to cause as much disruption as possible, drawing troops from the cities in response to smaller incursions. In this case, if you wish to run the scenario despite the Characters running behind Gideon’s preferred schedule, you could still rationalise the defence of Diesdorf as an unintended consequence of Gideon’s rousing the Red Crown.

Diesdorf.name: Diesdorf
Diesdorf.text:
Diesdorf lies south of Altdorf along the River Reik. It is famous as the home of the Diesdorf Military College. The town has an official population of 150 but that only includes officers of the rank of captain and above, property-owners, and master craftsmen, of which many are blacksmith and armourers supporting the college. The true population stands nearer 1600.

Diesdorf is also famous for its wheat fields; the economy of the town and surrounding areas relies heavily on a successful crop. The grain is mainly traded downriver to Altdorf, with the very best selected for the imperial household. The Magnus Corn Exchange stands at the centre of the town. Merchants buy and trade every Marktag.

The town also attracts a large number of Sigmarite pilgrims every year. This began soon after Magnus the Pious gave a legendary speech to the crowds gathered here.

The stone where Magnus is said to have stood, the Empire Stone, stands in the centre of Magnus Platz. A number of artists make a good living from sketching pilgrims standing atop the stone with a sword in hand.

Diesdorf has many more shrines to Sigmar than one would expect for a town of its size. Most families in Diesdorf have at least one member serving in the cult of Sigmar. It is also a common location for older or wounded priests of Sigmar to spend their waning years. There they continue to serve; caretaking shrines, helping maintain order, and training officers

The town is directly ruled by the Emperor. His representative is the Baronet Diesdorf, who is usually a senior retired military officer. The baronet does not hold an official post in the College and this sometimes leads to tension between the two. Yesterday morning, the baronet was killed when his breakfast of devilled eggs was poisoned. His was the first of a number of assassinations as @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-dotr.journals.uHClvCto8icrUp9P]{the Red Crown} tried to seize control of the town.

The baronet rules through the council, which consists of the following standing members:

  • A representative from the cult of Sigmar (murdered on the temple steps)

  • A representative from the other cults (currently Sister Cordula Kurtz from the cult of Shallya)

  • Two representatives from the Craft Guilds, these posts are held by the Armourers’ and Blacksmiths’ Guilds ( Johann Pielstock represents the Craftsmen, the second representative, Grandmaster Detlef Rotlander, disappeared after leading the coup.)

  • The senior College Officer (@UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain Theocritus von Hayek})

  • A representative from the Merchants’ Guild, a recent and much-debated addition (murdered in the street)

Diesdorf Military College

The Grand Reikland Imperial Military Officer Cadet Academy, founded by Emperor Wilhelm III in 2440 IC, is one of the most renowned and successful cadet schools in the Empire. It is more commonly known as the Diesdorf Military College or, to those that have studied and worked there, ‘The Dies’. The Imperial Treasury funds the school — in theory, entry is not reserved for the wealthy. The college attracts people already serving in the military whose talents for leadership have not gone unnoticed, and entry requires only a recommendation from a superior. The college is home to a number of small societies that are usually restricted to officers from nobility and often with the direct aim of making life difficult for their lower-class comrades.

There is an annual intake of 180 cadets. See @UUID[.MNlAndguDDzcnUNF]{Handout 1, the Quartermaster’s report}, for details of their disposition.

The college’s commandant is @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain Theocritus von Hayek}. His rank is that of colonel, but tradition means that he is referred to as captain, leading to confusion among the new cadets and a few good laughs for the veterans.

Down Diesdorf

Down Diesdorf, or simply ‘the Down’, lies outside of the town walls. What started as home to a few camp followers has grown into a sprawling area of ramshackle wooden buildings and the occasional tent. Everything here is geared towards taking money from the cadets, whether it is new weapons, uniforms, provisions, or an evening’s entertainment. On the weekends, the cadets come to the Down to party; the Keep-Down Patrol keeps relative order in the place. The patrol is an informal group consisting of priests of Sigmar, the Watch, and ex-officers. They tour the Down with clubs in hand and make sure no serious harm comes to anyone.

The Down and parts of the main town are dominated by the Havilund and Frankle crime families. They have a long history of conflict and are always ready to kill to protect their territory. The college and town at large mostly ignore them as long as they do not threaten either. Both families remember the Hurrtens, a crime family who got too ambitious and were killed or imprisoned within a week. The Havilunds and Frankles are also involved in smuggling contraband into Altdorf and sometimes make use of cadets who need money or their secrets kept secret.

Secrets in the Temples

The cellars of the Temple of Shallya hide a room only the clerics are allowed to enter. Inside are ten locals suffering from contagious @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.QiHMX5OyXBhWCYoF]{Ratte Fever}. Should they escape, the disease would have Diesdorf by the throat.

A captured Beastman is chained and guarded in the dungeons of the Temple of Sigmar. He is an old and dangerous Gor and the Clerics call him Red for the colour of the thick hair that covers his body. One of his Chaos gifts is the ability to influence the minds of others but this is currently hampered by Sigmarite blessings.

The Mind of Red

The Beastman known as Red is held captive beneath the Temple of Sigmar and has a subtle but terrible Chaos gift. The magics that protect the temple dampen this power but if Red is moved elsewhere it will begin to manifest.

Once the protection is lost, any human within 20 feet of Red for more than 12 hours must make a Very Easy (+60) Willpower Test. Failure means that Red is able to control one person at a time.

Once per hour, those controlled by Red can be made to undertake any task. Each time Red forces them to do so, they must make a Willpower Test. You should decide on the difficulty of the test based on Red’s Command. For example:

  • Very Easy (+60): Victim asked to hurt themselves.

  • Easy (+40): Victim asked to attack someone else (when they are not used to doing so).

  • Average (+20): Victim asked to attack someone else (when they are a solider).

  • Challenging: Victim asked to commit an act of sabotage without too much risk to themselves.

After the action is complete or the victim has successfully resisted, then Red’s control comes to an end and the victim suffers the @UUID[JournalEntry.clDxAiIdJMx0nLdC.JournalEntryPage.5vz04rkvAzyWaGhp#rattled-condition]{Rattled condition}.

The Coming Horde

If any of them survived the events of Death on the Reik, the force is led by @UUID[Actor.2YjfKNdAtKcfdDq1]{Ulfhednar the Destroyer}, @UUID[Actor.wXB3Bam0z0kp45Ht]{Etelka Herzen}, or @UUID[Actor.NTvkBP3VP4dtBqM0]{Ernst Heidelmann}. Ulfhednar’s loyal Minotaur companion, @UUID[Actor.o4Tigb2IUzxySP16]{Crakatz}, may also be in the army but does not lead. These NPCs have increased in power since Death on the Reik.

The Remains of the Council

The Characters arrive shortly after the attempted coup and with news of the approaching army sweeping the streets — the town is in shock. Those that were considering leaving are changing their minds after hearing news of a nearby massacre of escaping Diesdorf citizens.

The three remaining council members, Captain Theocritus von Hayek, Sister Cordula Kurtz, and Guildmaster Johann Pielstock, are at odds with each other. The population looks to them for leadership but it is not forthcoming.

Captain Theocritus von Hayek

Captain von Hayek is an old soldier, retired from the army of Nordland after he lost his right arm to a Norscan’s axe. Theocritus is the son of a camp follower and an officer he never knew. He served twenty years in various mercenary companies, fighting across the Empire and beyond. He continually demonstrated his bravery and leadership, making friends with a number of influential nobles over the years. This led to the greatest honour of his life — the command of the Imperial College. He strives every day to prove himself worthy of the position. The position on the council was not as welcome and he has tried to avoid it as much as possible. After arriving in Diesdorf, Captain von Hayek married and had three children, something he thought would never happen. He is determined to ensure the safety of the Diesdorf for his family and their neighbours.

Von Hayek wears his military uniform at all times and is often surrounded by a group of aides. He gives orders quickly and clearly and expects them to be carried out to the letter. He remembers the names of all those he talks to and is popular amongst his subordinates.

With the horde approaching, von Hayek thinks that it is more important to supervise the defences rather than sit with the council. He thought that he could trust the council to get the job done but realised he needed to spur them to make important decisions.

Agenda

Von Hayek does not trust the surviving council members with important decisions.

He suspects that perpetrators of the coup still reside in Diesdorf, and does not want to promote any citizens to the council until he is sure the conspirators are dead or fled.

Despite his own experience as a soldier, von Hayek does everything that he can to avoid the military seizing control. In his days as a solider von Hayek saw the military take control of population centres, often with disastrous (if unintended) consequences, and he wants to avoid this. He believes that the Council will do a better job at looking after the population, including his own family.

Sister Cordula Kurtz

As with many of those called to the service of Shallya, Kurtz was idealistic and a little naive. After her family starved to death in a famine, she thought she could change the world with healing hands. Thirty years later she has come to believe that this was just a foolish dream. However, on some days, her faith shines through and she believes that maybe small gifts of love and healing can make a difference. Kurtz had been in charge of the small Shallyan temple in Diesdorf for five years when the offer came to sit on the council, filling a seat usually held by the cult of Verena.

Short and stocky, Kurtz’s hair is pure white. She wears her robes of office with a simple dove amulet. Kurtz has grown to relish the power the council gives her. However, she is often outvoted, especially regarding how the lower classes are treated. Although she normally manages to remain calm, she has found that she is losing her temper more and more with the others on the council who she finds so frustrating.

Agenda

Kurtz aims to temper the judgement of the others with mercy and pity.

She seeks to give a voice to the poor.

Kurtz seeks to show that Shallyans should not be expected to be meek; she has as much right to voice opinions as anyone else.

Guildmaster Johann Pielstock

The third son of a woodcutter, the life of a woodsman did not suit Pielstock. His father realised he would be trouble and apprenticed him to a craftsman in Diesdorf. It took Pielstock years to understand the sacrifice his father made in sending him away. Although he never saw him again, he did make contact with his family a few years ago.

Although it was clear that his new master only wanted him for menial jobs, Pielstock demonstrated real skill and in time became his senior apprentice. However, becoming a fully qualified craftsman was more difficult. The snobbery of his master and others meant that members of the Guild did not want him. However, he had spent a lot of time arguing at the Guild for the rights of apprentices and, as his peers became members, he eventually had the support he needed.

Over the years Pielstock rose through the ranks. The highlight of his career came during a dispute with Dwarf guildmates. One of the senior Dwarfs grabbed him at a meeting and Pielstock knocked him unconscious. This earned the immediate respect of the Dwarfs who have been close allies ever since and meant that the reputation of Diesdorf crafts has risen higher than ever.

When attending council meetings Pielstock dresses smartly and is well groomed, always displaying the guild’s seal. His smart appearance cannot quite conceal a life of hard graft; his hands are rough, scarred, and calloused.

Agenda

Pielstock seeks to moderate any conflicts between middle-class business interests, poorer labourers, and Diesdorf ’s Dwarfs.

He seeks to help woodsmen and other people in the surrounding settlements, many of whom are poor and badly treated by their so-called betters.

Pielstock’s wife and children live in the Triangle, one of the better parts of town. He cannot afford for anything to happen to his house or he will be ruined.

An Offer that you Cannot Refuse

On arrival, @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain von Hayek} takes the Characters to a small meeting room and provides them with simple but tasty refreshments. Looking like a man with the weight of the world on his shoulders, he asks them to join the council.

‘Friends, like Magnus coming to save the Empire, Sigmar has sent you at this hour of need. Word of your deeds preceded your arrival. I have orders to notify Altdorf so that an Imperial River Boat can be sent, but until then I wish to ask a favour of you. The baronet and most of the town council were murdered in an attempted coup. The council is responsible for the defence of the city, and a great horde comes to destroy Diesdorf. While my soldiers can prepare the defences, there is much we cannot do. Your experience, fame, and skills mean that we stand a chance in preparing the town for what comes. Will you help us?’

The captain is honest in what he says but is concerned that the surviving council members will not do what needs to be done to protect Diesdorf. He knows that his decision is unpopular with others who would normally have expected to join the council, but von Hayek has told them that they need to wait for the new baronet.

If they agree, the Characters are taken to the temporary council chambers on the top floor of the college building to meet @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#sister-cordula-kurtz]{Sister Kurtz} and @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#guildmaster-johann-pielstock]{Guildmaster Pielstock}. The Characters are expected to take part in council meetings and are provided with small clean rooms nearby.

When the baronet is present the council is strictly advisory. When they are not, those present in the chamber may vote, with a majority required to win. A number of events that take place over the coming days are listed below. Each of the events where a vote may be required shows the expected votes of the standing council members. The Characters can change these votes with their actions. They can use Charm or Intimidate to influence the council. However, if these Skills are overused, it may antagonise the other council members (these Tests should start as Average (+20) but get progressively harder every time they are attempted). @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain van Hayek} only votes if the council is deadlocked and is very unhappy every time he has to do so.

Events at Diesdorf.name: Events at Diesdorf
Events at Diesdorf.text:
The following is a list of events occurring in the town before and during the Characters’ stay. Some of these events are labelled ‘Report’, meaning that information is provided to the council but no decision is necessary. Others are labelled ‘Decision’ meaning that the council are presented with a dilemma and must deliberate or vote to decide their course of action.

The Day Before the Characters Arrive

  • The nearby village of Rottfurt is razed with few survivors.

  • The few scouts that return report a vast horde only days away.

  • Refugees from surrounding settlements scramble for safety inside the town walls.

  • The coup is attempted, it fails but members of the council and college officials are killed.

  • Council placed under protective guard in the Military College.

Day One – The Character’s Arrive

  • The Quartermaster Reports — A report on the disposition of Diesdorf’s defences.

  • A Prisoner — A report that a Beastman is being kept beneath the town’s Temple of Sigmar.

  • The Herald — A messenger delivers the Red Crown’s demands, leading to a decision.

  • The Scouts — Bert Blum, chief scout, gives an account of destruction wrought by the horde, leading to a decision.

  • Komission of Public Works — Rumours of spies in the form of rats leads to a decision.

  • The Theatre — Diesdorf’s theatre gets a bad review, leading to a decision.

Day 2

  • Good Citizens — A group of townsfolk want to capitulate, leading to a decision.

  • The Walls of Diesdorf — Engineers produce findings about the town’s walls, leading to a decision.

  • The Traitor in Our Midst — Captain von Hayek gives a report on a disturbing letter.

  • Ruined Food Stocks — A report that town food supplies are running out.

  • Bring Down The Down — A request to level the Down leads to a decision.

  • Diseased — Infected refugees arrive, leading to a decision.

  • The Dwarfs — The council receives a report that anti-Dwarf sentiment is being stirred up.

  • Brustellite Uprising — There’s a report of a revolutionary group that have stormed the Temple of Sigmar.

  • Thieves — Report reaches the council of refugees caught stealing food, they may choose between clemency and harshness.

  • A Cunning Plan — The council are informed of a possible ruse to employ, leading to a decision.

Day 3

  • Mutiny — Based on previous decisions, units from Diesdorf’s military may mutiny.

  • Dwarf Elder — Diesdorf’s Dwarfs seek the support of the council, leading to a decision.

  • The Prisoner — The leader of the militia mutiny is dragged before the council, leading to a decision.

  • The Late Ones — A group of refugees arrive after dark, leading to a decision.

  • The Dwarf Engineer — An old dam could be flooded, leading to a decision.

  • The Collaborator — The townsfolk demand hanging a traitor, leading to a decision.

  • Disease — If refugees were allowed in earlier, the council hear a report of disease breaking out in Diesdorf.

  • The Saboteur — A saboteur may have been able to sneak in. If so, the council receives a report of the destruction of more food.

Day 4

  • Dwarf Elder — Diesdorf’s Dwarfs seek protection from the council, leading to a decision.

  • The Engineer — A skilled engineer gives recommendations, leading to a decision.

  • The Second Herald — A report of another messenger from the Red Crown seeking to intimidate the townsfolk.

  • Assassination — The Brustellites may launch a shocking attack, leading to a decision.

  • Helmut Brask — A delegation ask the council to issue a religious proclamation, leading to a decision.

  • The Adventurers — A chained group of individuals are dragged in front of the council, leading to a decision.

  • Pilgrims — A priest of Ulric asks for help, leading to a decision.

Day 5

  • The Red Crown horde arrives and loots the outskirts of Diesdorf.

  • The Trap — If the council permitted the cunning plan on Day 2, it is resolved at this point.

Day 6

  • The Attack

Preparing For War.name: Preparing For War
Preparing For War.text:
Day One

An airy but modest meeting room is set aside in the college for the councillors. They assemble here whenever a report is made or a decision presents itself. When the council is not in session, Captain von Hayek patrols the walls and inspects his troops, @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#sister-cordula-kurtz]{Cordula Kurtz} helps out at the shrine of Shallya, and @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#guildmaster-johann-pielstock]{Johann Pielstock} spreads his time between his townhouse in the Triangle, the docks, and various businesses in Diesdorf.

The Characters can spend their free time however they like, but are watched at all times by members of the Diesdorf garrison. @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Von Hayek} explains that this is for their protection and so they can be alerted if they need to return to council rooms. Whilst the captain is worried about conspirators hiding amongst the townsfolk, he also wants to ensure the Characters do not bring him into disrepute. The townsfolk are somewhat in awe of the Characters, and tend to be moderately Sigmarite in outlook.

PUT THEM TO WORK!

During the preparation for the attack, there are several occasions where the Council must decide whether to put the military or citizens to work. @UUID[.MNlAndguDDzcnUNF]{The Quartermaster’s report} details the numbers available. However, while they provide essential resource, they each come with challenges.

Summary of available resource, in order of efficiency:

140 Cadets plus officers: The cadets are an efficient and well-ordered workforce. However, both officers and cadets resent being used for jobs they see as beneath them. They become surly and resentful unless made to see how important it is.

200 Militia: A well-ordered and willing workforce, they work efficiently with minimal management. However, undertaking manual labour may affect their preparations for defending the town.

120 Watch: Although a largely willing workforce, taking the watch from their duties has an impact on law and order in the town.

40 additional citizens a day from refugees: Glad of being sheltered in the town, and often with first-hand knowledge of what is coming, they do whatever is needed.

600 citizens: Although willing to take part once they see the necessity of doing so, they need to be well managed. If they see, or think they see, others not doing their share then they become resentful and argumentative.

Votes are cast by drawing a cross or tick on a piece of paper and dropping it into a basket on the meeting room table. This means they are mostly anonymous and NPCs do not necessarily need to explain their reasons for voting the way they do.

The Quartermaster Reports

Shortly after the Characters take their seats on the council and discuss the situation, Sgt Albertus, the College Quartermaster, delivers a report on the resources that are available to the council. Albertus reads his report, salutes, and then leaves the written version (see 'Put them to Work' above for a summary, or @UUID[.MNlAndguDDzcnUNF]{full Handout}).

@UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain von Hayek} tells the councillors that he has ordered a report into the defences, which should be made tomorrow.

A Prisoner

Rikki Laubrich is a senior cleric of Sigmar in Diesdorf. He reports to the council that a Beastman is being held prisoner in the Temple of Sigmar. The creature was captured in a fight and is securely chained and guarded in his cell. The Sigmarites say he is of no danger at all — the clerics believe he has information that is useful to the cult of Sigmar so he is due to be taken to Altdorf.

The Scouts

Bert Blum, Diesdorf ’s chief scout, comes before the council dusty and dripping with sweat. He bends his knee and reports on what he has found:

The village of Rottfurt has been destroyed.

The horde is gathering for a push northwards, but parts of it are on the move towards Diesdorf. He and his experienced military scouts still estimate that they intend to march on Diesdorf.

He gives an accurate report about the army leaders (see @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#the-coming-horde]{The Coming Horde}).

Five Diesdorf scouts are missing, presumed dead.

Blum wants to know if the scouts should continue to observe or if there are any new orders. Pielstock suggests the scouts withdraw to the safety of town. (For: Kurtz, Pielstock. Against: von Hayek)

The Herald

A mutated figure is dragged before the council in chains. The creature has the head of a bird of prey and three arms. A symbol of a red crown is scratched into the flesh of his forearm. The Commander of the Watch announces that this is a herald from the Chaos army; his escort waits outside the gates. If allowed to speak, the mutant says:

‘I have come to offer a parley between my mistress, the Great Changer’s true voice in this land, and the burghers of the town of Diesdorf. My lady expects the gates to be open to her when her forces arrive. One out of every three citizens will be stood before the gates to serve her exaltedness and all within will offer worship to the gods of Chaos. If these conditions are not met, Diesdorf will be razed to the ground. The good citizens will be slaughtered, their servants fed to the mounts of the army … or to the army itself. What say you?’

@UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#sister-cordula-kurtz]{Sister Kurtz} and @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#guildmaster-johann-pielstock]{Guildmaster Pielstock} say that perhaps the town should consider the offer and that perhaps the Characters could negotiate more favourable terms. They do not vote for surrender unless the Characters do so first. In the unlikely event Diesdorf accepts the deal, Captain von Hayek moves to arrest the council and expel the Characters from the town.

The Theatre

Marte Brandauer and Eidsvik Buttgereit, two elderly but low-ranked clerics of Sigmar, come before the council. They petition to have the Sinkel Theatre burned to the ground. It has a thoroughly deserved reputation for staging productions that border on the blasphemous and Konrad Sinkel, the playwright and director, is known for his revolutionary views and commitment to artistic freedom. They say this is one of the reasons that Sigmar has abandoned the town. (For: Kurtz. Against: Pielstock, von Hayek)

If the Characters do not suggest it first, Kurtz wonders if the theatre might be spared in exchange for requiring Konrad to produce an uplifting religious epic. If the council order such a play, this has a positive effect, as Konrad chooses Sigmar at the Pass: An Epic of Seven Parts.

If nothing is done, the pair return once every afternoon to complain again, joined each time by more citizens.

Komission of Public Works

Diesdorf is rather small to have organised Komissions but an old engineer called Klaus Kopp logs issues with the town’s amenities and is affectionately known as the Komission of Public Works. He says that the local ratcatchers have noticed the rats are behaving strangely (he cannot say how) but certain ratcatchers believe that they are spying for the Chaos horde. Klaus would like the funds to increase the bounty on rats.

If the council agree to this, the poster below (@UUID[.D3hIjzYD63FJNQeN]{Handout 2}) appears on the streets and causes a bit of a panic and a rush to kill rats. (For: Kurtz, von Hayek. Against: Pielstock)

Day Two

Good Citizens

A group of citizens comes before the council and says that they want the town to surrender to the army. They believe that the council should offer the surrender of the town in exchange for its obedience to the horde. (Against: von Hayek, Kurtz, Pielstock)

If their first request is not granted they go on to ask that the gates be closed to refugees. They argue that the town is full and that the refugees are causing trouble. (Against: von Hayek, Kurtz, Pielstock)

The Walls of Diesdorf

Kar Ironfist, a Dwarf engineer, and Sven Jager, a Human engineer, come to report their findings as ordered by @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain von Hayek}. They say they believe that most of the town walls are secure. Jager says that he believes there is a problem with the North and South Gates. Both were designed to be blocked in case of attack, with the Dock Gate left as the only entrance to the town. Shooters Gate was built later, and cannot be blocked in this manner.

They recommend workers block the North and South Gates, otherwise they may be vulnerable. It will take three hundred workers, with a maximum of one hundred workers a day, to undertake this task. If the council uses soldiers, the military get upset, and if citizens are used the council become very unpopular. (For: von Hayek. Against: Kurtz, Pielstock)

If the works begin on the gates, the Shooters Gate and Dock Gate start to become crowded with refugees. This leads to disturbances and complaints from merchants living near the Temple of Sigmar.

Just before a decision is made, @UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain von Hayek} is called away by uniformed soldiers, who inform him of the potential traitor (see below). He returns after fifteen minutes.

The Traitor in Our Midst

@UUID[.aw43wUbMmf9SOaQv#captain-theocritus-von-hayek]{Captain von Hayek}, grave-faced, comes before the council. He says that this morning a keen-eyed watchman noticed that yesterday one of the Herald’s escorts passed a message to one of the other guards. This man was followed and interrogated before dying this morning. Von Hayek produces a parchment (@UUID[.ECUScHBPId6HPK4Q]{Handout 3}) that at one stage had been folded many times and has a slightly strange odour of damp and decay.

Von Hayek says ‘I have considered placing Kurtz and Pielstock under arrest to be tortured. However, I hope with the aid of our friends here that the actions of one traitor can be countered by the others. Should the council’s decisions be compromised, action may be required.’ He does not give any heed to those who point out that he is also a member of the council.

The letter was intended to be discovered and is simply a ploy to try and distract and divide the council.

Ruined Food Stocks

Albertus Hintz, one of the council scribes, reports that after closer examination, the grain stocks in the town silos are running low. Although they are largely full, they have been poorly maintained. Much has been ruined by damp and rats. Without resupply, the stores will only last a couple of days.

Bring Down the Down

The Commander of the City Guard, Axel Haack, asks for the Down to be demolished to allow the defenders clear line of fire on attackers from the west. Haack fears the enemy could take cover in the area otherwise. (For: von Hayek. Against: Kurtz, Pielstock)

This would take one thousand worker days to complete. For example, five hundred workers would take two days to manage this.

Demolishing the Down is a very unpopular decision. Those living in the Down include influential guild members, criminals, family members, and friends of those living inside the walls. They petition the council each day for the work to stop.

Diseased

A group of refugees are stopped at Shooters Gate. One of the guards noticed a number of them are diseased. A physician believes it is the contagious @UUID[Compendium.wfrp4e-core.items.UAwTqZ3hqNb7vq9s]{Itching Pox}. The council are asked whether they can enter. (For: Kurtz. Against: Pielstock, von Hayek)

If the refugees are refused entry, they have to be forced away from the town. If any overt harm comes to the refugees, there is unrest in the town.
